Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). content.content:
# CodeMySpec — Agent Workflow Guide

CodeMySpec is a requirements-driven development harness. It models your project as a
graph of **stories**, **components**, and **requirements**, then guides you through
building each piece in the right order: specs → tests → implementations → reviews → QA.

## Prerequisite: Phoenix project root

CodeMySpec is attached to a **Phoenix project root** — the folder containing
`mix.exs` with `:phoenix` in its deps. The harness reads `mix.exs`, walks
`lib/`, and writes specs, rules, and BDD files relative to that directory.
If a future session ever attaches to the wrong directory, the init checklist
surfaces it loudly; the user-side fix is to relaunch Claude Code from the
project root.

## Core Loop

```
get_next_requirement → start_task → do the work → (auto-evaluate) → repeat
```

### Step 1: Get Your Next Requirement

Call **`get_next_requirement`**. It syncs the filesystem, computes the requirement graph,
and returns the single highest-priority unsatisfied requirement whose prerequisites are met.

Three possible responses:
- **init_required** — project not linked yet. Follow the bootstrap checklist.
- **sync_required** — project exists but has no stories/components. Create them first.
- **next requirement** — the requirement to work on, with entity type, name, and ID.

### Step 2: Start the Task

Call **`start_task`** with the requirement's `requirement_name`, `entity_type`, and
`entity_id` (or `module_name` for components). This creates a task on your session and
returns a **detailed work prompt** containing:

- Which files to read (specs, rules, existing code)
- The exact file path to write to
- Templates and format requirements
- Design rules and coding standards for the component type
- Similar components to reference for patterns

**Follow the prompt.** It is tailored to the specific component and requirement.

### Step 3: Do the Work

The requirement types you'll encounter, in dependency order:

| Requirement | What You Produce |
|---|---|
| `spec_file` | Module specification in `.code_my_spec/spec/` |
| `spec_valid` | Fix validation errors in the spec |
| `review_file` | Design review for a context and its children |
| `review_valid` | Fix validation errors in the review |
| `test_file` | Test file following TDD — write tests before implementation |
| `test_spec_alignment` | Ensure tests cover all spec assertions |
| `implementation_file` | Implementation code in `lib/` |
| `tests_passing` | Fix failing tests |
| `bdd_specs_exist` | BDD scenario files for a story's acceptance criteria |
| `bdd_specs_passing` | Fix failing BDD specs |
| `qa_complete` | QA brief and results for a story |

### Step 4: Automatic Evaluation

When you finish (or the session stops), the harness evaluates your output:
- Does the file exist at the expected path?
- Does it parse/validate against the document schema?
- Do tests compile and pass?
- Is the test aligned with the spec's assertions?

If evaluation finds problems, you receive structured feedback. Fix and continue.

## Project Structure

```
.code_my_spec/
├── architecture/     Component graph, dependency diagram, decisions
├── spec/             Module specifications (*.spec.md)
├── rules/            Design and test rules by component type
├── status/           Implementation status per component
├── issues/           Known bugs (incoming/, accepted/, dismissed/)
├── knowledge/        Project-specific research
├── framework/        Framework reference docs
├── design/           Design system assets
├── qa/               QA briefs, results, journey plans
└── integrations/     Integration specs
```

## MCP Tools Reference

### Requirements & Tasks
| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `get_next_requirement` | Get the next thing to work on |
| `start_task` | Begin work — returns the detailed prompt |
| `list_requirements` | See all requirements and their status |
| `sync_project` | Re-sync filesystem state |
| `evaluate_task` | Manually trigger evaluation |
| `list_tasks` | See active/completed tasks |

### Stories & Architecture
| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `list_stories` / `list_story_titles` | View user stories |
| `set_story_component` | Link a story to its surface component |
| `analyze_stories` | Analyze stories for architecture mapping |
| `validate_dependency_graph` | Check for circular dependencies |

### Issues
| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `list_issues` / `get_issue` | View issues |
| `create_issue` | Report a new issue |
| `accept_issue` / `dismiss_issue` | Triage incoming issues |
| `resolve_issue` | Mark an issue as fixed |

### Bootstrap (first-time setup)
| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `list_projects` | See available projects |
| `init_project` | Link this directory to a project |
| `install_claude_md` | Create/update CLAUDE.md managed section |
| `install_agents_md` | Create/update this file |
| `install_rules` | Copy design and test rules |

## Component Types

The harness supports these component types, each with their own requirement
chain and design rules:

- **context** — Domain boundary with public API (`.code_my_spec/rules/context_design.md`)
- **schema** — Data structure with validation (`.code_my_spec/rules/schema_design.md`)
- **repository** — Data access layer (`.code_my_spec/rules/repository_design.md`)
- **liveview** — Phoenix LiveView page (`.code_my_spec/rules/liveview_design.md`)
- **liveview_component** — Reusable LiveView component (`.code_my_spec/rules/liveview_component_design.md`)
- **live_context** — LiveView grouping (spec + review only)
- **controller** — Phoenix HTTP handler
- **genserver** — Stateful process
- **task** — Background job
- **behaviour** — Callback definition (spec + implementation only)

General Elixir rules: `.code_my_spec/rules/elixir_design.md`, `.code_my_spec/rules/elixir_test.md`

## Key Principles

1. **The graph is the plan.** Don't decide what to work on — ask `get_next_requirement`.
2. **Specs before code.** Every component gets a specification first. Tests are written
   from the spec. Implementation satisfies the tests.
3. **Read the task prompt.** It contains everything you need: templates, rules, file paths,
   and patterns from similar components.
4. **One requirement at a time.** Complete it, let evaluation run, then get the next one.
5. **Issues are first-class.** If you find a problem, create an issue. Don't fix unrelated
   things inline.

## Architecture Reference

| Need | File |
|---|---|
| Component graph with types and deps | `.code_my_spec/architecture/overview.md` |
| Namespace hierarchy | `.code_my_spec/architecture/namespace_hierarchy.md` |
| Dependency diagram (Mermaid) | `.code_my_spec/architecture/dependency_graph.mmd` |
| Architecture decisions | `.code_my_spec/architecture/decisions/` |
| Implementation status | `.code_my_spec/status/cleaner_crm.md` |

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # No `:protect_from_forgery` — unlike the GET-only public routes below
  # (which can just use `:browser`), `/pay/:token` accepts a POST from a
  # client with no session and no CSRF token (a mailed or shared link).
  # `:fetch_current_scope_for_user` still runs — the root layout reads
  # `@current_scope` unconditionally, and this plug assigns `nil` when
  # no one's logged in rather than requiring an authenticated visitor.
  pipeline :public do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :webhook do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # Office-only controller routes (e.g. the payroll CSV export) layer
  # this on top of `:require_authenticated_user`; office-only
  # LiveViews use the equivalent `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole`
  # on_mount hook instead, since a plug can't gate a live_session.
  pipeline :require_office_role do
    plug CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index

      live "/field", FieldLive.Today, :index
      live "/field/jobs/:id", FieldLive.Job, :show
    end

    # Office-only surfaces: dispatch, payroll, quality, invoicing,
    # clients, quotes, reminders, and the audit trail. Gated to
    # owners/admins by `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole` — a cleaner
    # is redirected to `/field` instead. See that module for why it's
    # a separate `live_session` from the one above.
    live_session :require_office_role,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
      ] do
      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new

      live "/audit", AuditLive, :index

      live "/quotes", QuoteLive.Index, :index
      live "/quotes/new", QuoteLive.Builder, :new
      live "/quotes/:id", QuoteLive.Builder, :show

      live "/quality", QualityLive.Review, :index
      live "/quality/scorecards", QualityLive.Scorecards, :index
      live "/quality/templates", QualityLive.Templates, :index
      live "/quality/templates/new", QualityLive.Templates, :new
      live "/quality/templates/:id/edit", QualityLive.Templates, :edit
      live "/quality/:job_id", QualityLive.Review, :show

      live "/timesheets", TimesheetLive, :index

      live "/invoices", InvoiceLive.Index, :index
      live "/invoices/:id", InvoiceLive.Show, :show

      live "/reminders", ReminderLive, :index
    end

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user, :require_office_role]

    get "/timesheets/export", TimesheetExportController, :show
  end

  scope "/integrations/oauth", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
    get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new
      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete

    # Public confirm/reschedule links a client reaches from their
    # reminder — no login, so `:browser` (not `:require_authenticated_user`)
    # like the routes above. Plain `:browser`, not `:public`, so
    # `fetch_current_scope_for_user` still assigns `current_scope` for
    # the root layout.
    get "/reminders/confirm/:token", ReminderController, :confirm
    get "/reminders/reschedule/:token", ReminderController, :reschedule
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :public

    get "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :show
    post "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :create
  end

  scope "/webhooks", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :webhook

    post "/stripe", StripeWebhookController, :create
    post "/twilio", TwilioWebhookController, :status
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm do
  @moduledoc """
  CleanerCrm keeps the contexts that define your domain
  and business logic.

  Contexts are also responsible for managing your data, regardless
  if it comes from the database, an external API or others.
  """

  # Fixture modules live in test/support and only compile in :test —
  # exporting them unconditionally warns in dev.
  @test_only_exports (if Mix.env() == :test do
                        [ClientsFixtures, SchedulingFixtures, UsersFixtures]
                      else
                        []
                      end)

  use Boundary,
    deps: [],
    # CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() is invoked to build absolute links for
    # outbound emails and OAuth redirect URIs (invitation emails, OAuth
    # provider config) — the standard phx.gen.auth-style exception.
    dirty_xrefs: [CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint],
    exports:
      @test_only_exports ++
        [
          Accounts,
          Accounts.Account,
          Accounts.Invitation,
          Accounts.Member,
          Accounts.MembersRepository,
          Audit,
          Audit.AuditEntry,
          Authorization,
          Billing,

          Billing.Payment,
          Clients,
          Clients.Client,
          Clients.Property,
          Codemyspec.Client,
          Users,
          Users.User,
          Users.Scope,
          Integrations,
          Integrations.OAuthStateStore,
          Mailer,
          Money,
          Notifications,
          Notifications.Notification,
          Notifications.ReminderSettings,
          Quality,
          Quality.Checklist,
          Quality.ChecklistItem,
          Quality.ChecklistTemplate,
          Quality.IncidentReport,
          Quality.Photo,
          Quality.Scorecard,
          Quoting,
          Quoting.Pricing,
          Quoting.Quote,

          Quoting.RateCard,
          Repo,
          Scheduling,
          Scheduling.AvailabilityBlock,
          Scheduling.Job,
          Scheduling.RecurringPlan,
          TimeTracking,
          TimeTracking.Earnings,
          TimeTracking.PayRate,
          TimeTracking.TimeEntry
        ]
end

=== /Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm/test/spex/850_see_my_visits_cleaner_and_proof-of-work_in_a_client_portal/criterion_7251_client_opens_the_portal_via_a_valid_magic_link_spex.exs ===
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story850.Criterion7251Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 850 — See my visits, cleaner, and proof-of-work in a client portal
  Criterion 7251 — Client opens the portal via a valid magic link: the
  portal opens showing upcoming visits and service history, with no
  password required.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a valid magic-link token opens the client's portal" do
    scenario "client opens the portal via a valid magic link" do
      given_ "a client has been sent a magic-link token for their portal", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Morgan Blake"})
        session = Fixtures.portal_magic_link_fixture(client)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, session: session})}
      end

      when_ "the client follows the link", context do
        access_conn = get(context.conn, ~p"/portal/access/#{context.session.token}")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :access_conn, access_conn)}
      end

      then_ "the portal opens showing their upcoming visits and service history without requiring a password",
            context do
        assert redirected_to(context.access_conn) == ~p"/portal"

        {:ok, portal_live, _html} = context.access_conn |> recycle() |> live(~p"/portal")

        assert has_element?(portal_live, "[data-test='upcoming-visits']")
        assert has_element?(portal_live, "[data-test='service-history']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story850.Criterion7252Spex do
  @moduledoc """

  Criterion 7252 — Expired or invalid magic link denies access:
  access is denied and the client is offered a way to request a

  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "an expired magic-link token denies portal access" do
    scenario "expired or invalid magic link denies access" do
      given_ "a client's magic-link token has expired", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Morgan Blake"})

        session =

      end
    end
  end
end

  @moduledoc """

        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})
        cleaner = Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(scope, account, %{name: "Jamie Rivera"})
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Morgan Blake"})
        job = Fixtures.job_fixture(scope, client, %{cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
        conn = Fixtures.portal_session_fixture(client)

      end

=== /Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm/test/spex/850_see_my_visits_cleaner_and_proof-of-work_in_a_client_portal/criterion_7254_reassigning_the_cleaner_updates_what_the_client_sees_spex.exs ===
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story850.Criterion7254Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 850 — See my visits, cleaner, and proof-of-work in a client portal
  Criterion 7254 — Reassigning the cleaner updates what the client
  sees: the next time the portal is viewed, it shows the newly
  assigned cleaner.

  Reassignment is driven through the real dispatch board
  (`ScheduleLive.Board`, covered end-to-end by story 834's own
  reassignment specs), not seeded directly, since the board's
  cleaner-select is the actual mechanism that changes a job's
  assignment.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "reassigning a visit's cleaner is reflected the next time the portal is viewed" do
    scenario "reassigning the cleaner updates what the client sees" do
      given_ "a client's upcoming visit currently shows Cleaner A", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})
        cleaner_a = Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(scope, account, %{name: "Jamie Rivera"})
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Morgan Blake"})
        job = Fixtures.job_fixture(scope, client, %{cleaner_id: cleaner_a.id})
        portal_conn = Fixtures.portal_session_fixture(client)

        {:ok, portal_live, _html} = live(portal_conn, ~p"/portal")
        assert has_element?(portal_live, "[data-test='visit-#{job.id}']", cleaner_a.name)

        owner_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{
           scope: scope,
           account: account,
           cleaner_a: cleaner_a,
           client: client,
           job: job,
           portal_conn: portal_conn,
           owner_conn: owner_conn
         })}
      end

      when_ "the business reassigns the visit to Cleaner B", context do
        cleaner_b = Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{name: "Sam Okafor"})

        {:ok, board_live, _html} = live(context.owner_conn, ~p"/schedule")

        board_live
        |> element("[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-cleaner-select']")
        |> render_change(%{"cleaner_id" => to_string(cleaner_b.id)})

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :cleaner_b, cleaner_b)}
      end

      then_ "the client's portal shows Cleaner B's name and photo the next time it is viewed",
            context do
        {:ok, portal_live, _html} = live(context.portal_conn, ~p"/portal")

        assert has_element?(
                 portal_live,
                 "[data-test='visit-#{context.job.id}']",
                 context.cleaner_b.name
               )

        refute has_element?(
                 portal_live,
                 "[data-test='visit-#{context.job.id}']",
                 context.cleaner_a.name
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})
        cleaner_a = Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(scope, account, %{name: "Jamie Rivera"})

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures do
  @moduledoc """
  Curated bridge from BDD specs into in-app state.

  The only module that may dep on `CleanerCrm` from inside the spex test
  tree. Declared as its own top-level Boundary so the spec boundary
  (`CleanerCrmSpex`) can dep on it without inheriting `CleanerCrm`'s deps.

  Keep this list small — every export is a sanctioned shortcut past the
  UI, used only for `given_` state that has its own covered creation flow.
  """

  use Boundary, top_level?: true, deps: [CleanerCrm, CleanerCrmTest]

  # These contexts are specified in the architecture but not yet
  # implemented — the red BDD specs that call these fixtures exist to
  # drive their implementation. Remove entries as each context lands.
  @compile {:no_warn_undefined,
            [
              CleanerCrm.Clients,
              CleanerCrm.Scheduling,
              CleanerCrm.Booking,
              CleanerCrm.Portal,
              CleanerCrm.Reviews
            ]}

  # Auth/session seeding — registration and login have their own specs;
  # every other spec starts from an existing confirmed user.
  defdelegate user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate valid_user_password(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate set_password(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  # Tenant seeding — account creation has its own spec; other specs need
  # an existing company (account) to scope against.
  # Uncertain export: prune if account specs end up seeding via the UI.
  def account_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, account} =
      CleanerCrm.Accounts.create_account(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})
      )

    account
  end

  # Session — logs a fixture user into a conn. Login itself has its
  # own auth specs; every other spec starts from an authenticated conn.
  defdelegate log_in_user(conn, user), to: CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase

  # Scheduling (story 834) — a cleaner is an account member who gets
  # assigned jobs. No creation flow covers this yet: `ScheduleLive.Board`
  # (the board's own assign/reassign UI) doesn't exist. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — prune once the board can seed
  # cleaner assignment directly.
  def cleaner_fixture(scope, account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture(attrs)
    {:ok, _member} = CleanerCrm.Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account.id, :member)
    user
  end

  # Billing (story 836) — client, job, and invoice seeding.
  #
  # Job completion generating its invoice is covered end-to-end by
  # story 836's own "completing a job generates its invoice" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job -> InvoiceLive). Scenarios whose subject is
  # a downstream invoice-collection decision (charging a card,
  # payment links, declines, webhook confirmation) seed the completed
  # job and its invoice directly here instead of re-driving job
  # completion every time — a sanctioned shortcut per
  # bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def client_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, client} =
      CleanerCrm.Clients.create_client(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          name: "Client #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
          card_on_file: false,
          email: "client#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com",
          phone: "+15555550100"
        })
      )

    client
  end

  def job_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    attrs = Enum.into(attrs, %{})
    start_time = Map.get(attrs, :start_time, ~T[09:00:00])

    {:ok, job} =
      CleanerCrm.Scheduling.create_job(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
          status: :scheduled,
          scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),
          start_time: start_time,
          # Some specs override `start_time` alone (e.g. pinning it to a
          # lead-time boundary) without overriding `end_time` — a fixed
          # `~T[11:00:00]` default would then land before an overridden
          # start_time and fail the "end after start" changeset check.
          end_time: default_end_time(start_time)
        })
      )

    # Notifications (story 837) — the automatic reminder trigger is a
    # periodic Oban-cron scan in production (see the background-jobs
    # ADR); nothing about creating a job through this fixture would
    # otherwise run that scan within a spec's lifetime. Running it here
    # is a no-op for every job outside its owning account's configured
    # lead-time window (and a no-op entirely for accounts that never
    # configured reminders), so it's safe for every other story's jobs
    # while making story 837's own boundary-timed fixtures deterministic.
    CleanerCrm.Notifications.send_due_reminders()

    job
  end

  # `given_` blocks bind `scope` from `user_scope_fixture/1` *before*
  # `account_fixture/2` creates the account, so it never carries an
  # `active_account_id` — every fixture below that scopes a context
  # call by account needs to resolve it from the user's membership at
  # call time instead of trusting the scope it was handed.
  defp scoped_to_account(%CleanerCrm.Users.Scope{active_account_id: nil, user: user} = scope) do
    case CleanerCrm.Accounts.MembersRepository.list_user_accounts(user.id) do
      [account | _] -> %{scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}
      [] -> scope
    end
  end

  defp scoped_to_account(scope), do: scope

  # Two hours after `start_time`, unless that would wrap past midnight
  # (into an earlier clock time), in which case the day just ends there.
  defp default_end_time(start_time) do
    candidate = Time.add(start_time, 2 * 3600, :second)
    if Time.compare(candidate, start_time) == :gt, do: candidate, else: ~T[23:59:59]
  end

    job
  end

    invoice
  end

  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def time_entry_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, time_entry} =
      CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.create_time_entry(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 12:00:00Z]
        })
      )

    time_entry
  end

  # Notifications (story 837) — an already-sent appointment reminder
  # with its confirm/reschedule token.
  #
  # The automatic "reminder sent at the configured lead time" trigger
  # is covered end-to-end by story 837's own "reminder fires at the
  # configured lead time" spec. Scenarios whose subject is a
  # downstream decision on an existing reminder (confirm, reschedule,
  # delivery-status fallback) seed the already-sent notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the scheduler trigger every
  # time — a sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def notification_fixture(scope, client, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :reminder,
          channel: :email,
          status: :sent,
          token: "reminder_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Schedule alerts (story 843) — a pending schedule-change
  # notification already pushed to a cleaner.
  #
  # The push itself (a moved or cancelled job creating this
  # notification) is covered end-to-end by story 843's own "moved job
  # notifies the cleaner" / "cancelled job notifies the cleaner"
  # specs, which drive the real trigger via `ScheduleLive.Board`.
  # Scenarios whose subject is a downstream decision on an existing
  # pending change (acknowledging, re-prompting, office visibility,
  # escalation, channel fallback) seed the already-pushed notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the board move every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md. Never pass
  # `status: :acknowledged` here — the acknowledgment round-trip
  # through `FieldLive.Today` is the whole point of story 843.
  def schedule_change_notification_fixture(scope, cleaner, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :schedule_change,
          channel: :push,
          status: :pending,
          change_summary: "Job schedule changed",
          pushed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
          token: "schedule_change_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

  #
  # Checking items off and completing the job through the checklist UI
  # is the subject under test in `FieldLive.Job`, so this fixture stops
  # short of that — it only seeds the checklist itself. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md: `ChecklistTemplate` assignment
  # (story 842) has its own creation flow this fixture skips.
  def job_with_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, attrs \\ %{}) do

  # Quality (story 842) — a job carrying an unfinished, room-grouped

  def job_with_room_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, items, attrs \\ %{}) do

  # Quoting (story 848) — the account's public-facing rate card, set
  # directly rather than through the office `QuoteLive.Builder` rate
  # card form (covered end-to-end by story 835) since these specs'
  # subject is the public instant-quote calculator reading it, not the
  # office save flow. Extra keys the current `RateCard` schema doesn't
  # persist yet (frequency discounts, add-on pricing) are accepted
  # here so specs can drive the pricing config story 848 needs once
  # the schema grows to hold it.
  def rate_card_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope = scoped_to_account(scope)
    rate_card = CleanerCrm.Quoting.get_or_create_rate_card(scope)
    {:ok, rate_card} = CleanerCrm.Quoting.update_rate_card(scope, rate_card, attrs)
    rate_card
  end

  # Booking (story 849) — an instant quote already accepted by the
  # client (contact captured, price locked). The quote-to-accepted
  # transition itself is covered end-to-end by story 848's own
  # "instant quote price matches the later acceptance total" spec, so
  # scenarios whose subject is the slot/policy/card steps that follow
  # seed the accepted lead directly here instead of re-driving the
  # quote calculator every time — a sanctioned shortcut per
  # bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def lead_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, lead} =
      CleanerCrm.Booking.create_lead(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          pricing_model: :per_room,
          bedroom_count: 3,
          bathroom_count: 2,
          frequency: :one_time,
          total_cents: 19_500,
          status: :accepted,
          client_name: "Dana Prescott",
          client_email: "dana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com",
          client_phone: "+15555550100"
        })
      )

    lead
  end

  # Portal (story 850) — an already-issued, not-yet-exchanged
  # magic-link token for a client, distinct from `portal_session_fixture/1`
  # above (which bypasses straight to an established session for
  # downstream stories 851/852). This one's subject is the token
  # exchange itself — validity and expiry — so it hands back the raw
  # session/token record rather than a conn already carrying it.
  def portal_magic_link_fixture(client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, session} = CleanerCrm.Portal.create_portal_session(client, Enum.into(attrs, %{}))
    session
  end

  # Reviews (story 853) — an already-sent review request for a
  # completed visit, distinct from the thank-you/request send itself
  # (covered end-to-end by criteria 7244/7245's own specs). Scenarios
  # whose subject is what happens once the client reaches
  # `ReviewLive.Public` (rating routing, no-duplicate-request) seed
  # the already-requested review directly here instead of re-driving
  # the completion-to-request pipeline every time — a sanctioned
  # shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def review_request_fixture(scope, job, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, review} =
      CleanerCrm.Reviews.create_review(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          client_id: client.id,
          status: :review_requested,
          token: "review_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
          review_request_sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
        })
      )

    review
  end

  # Reviews (story 853) — runs the periodic review-request scan now,
  # exactly as `CleanerCrm.Reviews.ReviewScheduler.perform/1` does on
  # its Oban cron schedule (mirrors `send_due_reminders/0` above for
  # story 837's reminder scan). `as_of` lets a spec assert the
  # ~24h-later trigger without backdating any row's own timestamp —
  # the same injectable "now" seam `ReminderScheduler.scan_and_send/1`
  # already uses.
  def run_due_review_requests(as_of \\ DateTime.utc_now()) do
    CleanerCrm.Reviews.send_due_review_requests(as_of)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story852.Criterion7238Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 852 — Pay invoices and tip my cleaner from the portal
  Criterion 7238 — Client pays an invoice with a new card

  Per the payments-stripe ADR (see `CleanerCrm.Billing`'s moduledoc),
  a submitted charge only ever moves an invoice to `:charge_pending`
  — final `:paid` status is webhook-driven (criterion 7239). This
  spec's subject is the submission itself, so it asserts the
  submission's own confirmation and receipt rather than a final
  "Paid" status.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  import Swoosh.TestAssertions

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a client pays an invoice with a new card from the portal" do
    scenario "client pays an invoice with a new card" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "I have an unpaid invoice and no card on file", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{card_on_file: false})
        job = Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(context.scope, client)

        invoice =
          Fixtures.invoice_fixture(context.scope, job, %{
            amount: Decimal.new("150.00"),
            status: :unpaid
          })

        portal_conn = Fixtures.portal_session_fixture(client)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, invoice: invoice, portal_conn: portal_conn})}
      end

      when_ "I pay the invoice with a new card", context do
        {:ok, invoices_live, _html} = live(context.portal_conn, ~p"/portal/invoices")

        invoices_live
        |> element("[data-test='invoice-#{context.invoice.id}-pay-button']")
        |> render_click()

        invoices_live
        |> form("[data-test='invoice-#{context.invoice.id}-payment-form']",
          payment: %{card_token: "pm_card_visa"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :invoices_live, invoices_live)}
      end

      then_ "my payment is submitted for the full invoice amount", context do
        assert render(context.invoices_live) =~ "$150.00"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "I receive a receipt", context do
        assert_email_sent(to: context.client.email)

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

  @moduledoc """
  Story 852 — Pay invoices and tip my cleaner from the portal
  Criterion 7239 — Invoice marked paid on webhook confirmation

  The charge submission itself is covered by criterion 7238's spec;
  this spec's subject is the webhook-driven final transition, so the
  pending charge is seeded directly via `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures` and
  the webhook is posted the same way story 836's criterion 7158
  already proves for the owner-facing invoice.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a portal payment is only marked paid once the provider confirms it" do
    scenario "invoice marked paid on webhook confirmation" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "I submitted payment on an invoice and it's awaiting confirmation", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)
        job = Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(context.scope, client)

        invoice =
          Fixtures.invoice_fixture(context.scope, job, %{
            amount: Decimal.new("150.00"),
            status: :charge_pending,
            stripe_payment_intent_id: "pi_test_portal_succeeded_123"
          })

        portal_conn = Fixtures.portal_session_fixture(client)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, invoice: invoice, portal_conn: portal_conn})}
      end

      when_ "the provider confirms the charge succeeded", context do
        payload = %{
          "type" => "payment_intent.succeeded",
          "data" => %{
            "object" => %{
              "id" => context.invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id,
              "metadata" => %{"invoice_id" => to_string(context.invoice.id)}
            }
          }

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling do
  @moduledoc """
  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
  conflict-aware assignment.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Property
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{
    AvailabilityBlock,
    ConflictDetector,
    Job,
    Recurrence,
    RecurringPlan
  }

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  ## Jobs

  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job. Recorded in the audit trail as authored by the
  caller, unless `actor: :system` is passed — used when the job is one
  occurrence materialized from a recurring plan rather than a job a
  human directly asked for (see `create_recurring_plan/2`).
  """
  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           %Job{account_id: account_id}
           |> Job.changeset(derive_client_id(account_id, attrs))
           |> Repo.insert() do
      record_job_created(scope, job, Keyword.get(opts, :actor, :user))
      {:ok, job}
    end
  end

  # The board's own job form (and a recurring plan's own materialized
  # occurrences, via `Recurrence.job_attrs/1`) only ever carry a
  # `property_id` — never a `client_id` — so a job created either way
  # otherwise saves with `client_id: nil`. That breaks anything reading
  # the client straight off the job rather than through its property
  # (story 836's invoicing does both a card-on-file charge lookup and
  # the invoice's own client label this way), so every job creation
  # backfills `client_id` from its property here rather than requiring
  # every caller to remember to. A caller that already supplies a
  # `client_id` (fixtures with only a client on hand, no property) is
  # left alone.
  defp derive_client_id(account_id, attrs) do
    if blank?(fetch_attr(attrs, :client_id)) do
      case fetch_attr(attrs, :property_id) do
        value when value in [nil, ""] -> attrs
        property_id -> put_client_id_from_property(attrs, account_id, property_id)
      end
    else
      attrs
    end
  end

  defp put_client_id_from_property(attrs, account_id, property_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Property, id: property_id, account_id: account_id) do
      %Property{client_id: client_id} when not is_nil(client_id) ->
        # Match whichever key style (atom or string) `attrs` already
        # uses — `Ecto.Changeset.cast/4` raises on a map mixing both.
        if Map.has_key?(attrs, :property_id) do
          Map.put(attrs, :client_id, client_id)
        else
          Map.put(attrs, "client_id", client_id)
        end

      _ ->
        attrs
    end
  end

  defp fetch_attr(attrs, key), do: Map.get(attrs, key) || Map.get(attrs, to_string(key))

  defp blank?(nil), do: true
  defp blank?(""), do: true
  defp blank?(_value), do: false

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :system) do
    Recorder.record_system(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :user) do
    Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  # Deliberately omits `scheduled_date`: a "created" entry's own
  # subject label (job → property/client) is enough to identify which
  # job this is, and surfacing it here would read as a schedule change
  # (`field_changes/1`'s "Scheduled date: ..." line) indistinguishable
  # from an actual reschedule recorded later by `update_job/3`.
  defp job_created_values(job) do
    %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id}
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
  """
  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.

  `:include_cancelled_ids` (default `[]`) admits specific cancelled
  jobs back in anyway — the board's own escape hatch for a cancelled
  job that still carries an unacknowledged schedule-change
  notification (story 843): the office needs to keep seeing its
  ack-status until the cleaner acknowledges, and the escalation check
  needs the job rendered at all to ever run. Other callers passing no
  opts see the same non-cancelled set as before.
  """
  def list_jobs(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    include_cancelled_ids = Keyword.get(opts, :include_cancelled_ids, [])

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and
        (j.status != :cancelled or j.id in ^include_cancelled_ids)
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
  """
  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <-
           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
             scope,
             cleaner_id,
             job.scheduled_date,
             job.start_time,
             job.end_time,
             exclude_job_id: job.id
           ),
         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_reassigned",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_cancelled",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Updates a job's schedule and/or price — a reschedule, a price
  change, or both, made directly from the board rather than through
  `assign_cleaner/3`'s conflict-checked path. Records only the fields
  that actually changed to the audit trail, attributed to the caller.
  """
  def update_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    changeset = Job.changeset(job, derive_client_id(account_id, attrs))

    with {:ok, updated} <- Repo.update(changeset) do
      record_job_updated(scope, job, changeset, updated)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @audited_update_fields ~w(scheduled_date start_time end_time agreed_price_cents status)a

  defp record_job_updated(scope, job, changeset, updated) do
    changed_fields =
      changeset.changes
      |> Map.keys()
      |> Enum.filter(&(&1 in @audited_update_fields))

    if changed_fields != [] do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        update_action(changed_fields),
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        audit_snapshot(job, changed_fields),
        audit_snapshot(updated, changed_fields)
      )
    end
  end

  defp update_action(changed_fields) do
    cond do
      Enum.any?(changed_fields, &(&1 in [:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])) ->
        "job_rescheduled"

      :agreed_price_cents in changed_fields ->
        "job_price_changed"

      true ->
        "job_updated"
    end
  end

  defp audit_snapshot(job, fields),
    do: Map.new(fields, &{to_string(&1), audit_value(Map.get(job, &1))})

  defp audit_value(%Date{} = value), do: to_string(value)
  defp audit_value(%Time{} = value), do: to_string(value)
  defp audit_value(value), do: value

  @doc """
  Removes a job from the board without hard-deleting its row — the
  row (and any audit entries already about it) stays resolvable for
  the trail. Distinct from `cancel_job/2`: this is the office
  correcting a mistaken entry rather than calling off an appointment,
  so it's recorded as "deleted" rather than "cancelled" and never
  notifies the assigned cleaner.
  """
  def delete_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_deleted",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  ## Recurring plans

  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    RecurringPlan
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan, Recurrence.occurrences(plan))
  end

  @doc """
  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
  """
  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, plan} <-
             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
             |> Repo.insert() do
        jobs =
          plan
          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs, actor: :system)
            job
          end)

        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  ## Availability blocks

  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
  end

  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
  end

  @doc """
  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
  through.
  """
  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
      {:ok, user}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Fetches a single cleaner by id, for their detail page. Draws from
  the same membership list as `list_cleaners/1`, so a user who isn't
  a member of this account can't be looked up here either. Raises if
  not found.
  """
  def get_cleaner!(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    cleaner_id = parse_cleaner_id(id)

    scope
    |> list_cleaners()
    |> Enum.find(&(&1.id == cleaner_id))
    |> case do
      nil -> raise Ecto.NoResultsError, queryable: User
      cleaner -> cleaner
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Lists a cleaner's time-off blocks for their detail page, soonest
  first.
  """
  def list_availability_blocks(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    cleaner_id = parse_cleaner_id(cleaner_id)

    AvailabilityBlock
    |> where([b], b.account_id == ^account_id and b.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id)
    |> order_by([b], asc: b.date)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists a cleaner's upcoming (today or later, non-cancelled) jobs for
  their detail page, soonest first.
  """
  def list_upcoming_jobs_for_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    cleaner_id = parse_cleaner_id(cleaner_id)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and
        j.status != :cancelled and j.scheduled_date >= ^Date.utc_today()
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  defp parse_cleaner_id(id) when is_integer(id), do: id
  defp parse_cleaner_id(id) when is_binary(id), do: String.to_integer(id)

  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp placeholder_email(name) do
    slug =
      name
      |> String.downcase()
      |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, ".")
      |> String.trim(".")

    "#{slug}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@cleaners.local"
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling do
  @moduledoc """
  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
  conflict-aware assignment.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Property
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{
    AvailabilityBlock,
    ConflictDetector,
    Job,
    Recurrence,
    RecurringPlan
  }

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  ## Jobs

  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job. Recorded in the audit trail as authored by the
  caller, unless `actor: :system` is passed — used when the job is one
  occurrence materialized from a recurring plan rather than a job a
  human directly asked for (see `create_recurring_plan/2`).
  """
  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           %Job{account_id: account_id}
           |> Job.changeset(derive_client_id(account_id, attrs))
           |> Repo.insert() do
      record_job_created(scope, job, Keyword.get(opts, :actor, :user))
      {:ok, job}
    end
  end

  # The board's own job form (and a recurring plan's own materialized
  # occurrences, via `Recurrence.job_attrs/1`) only ever carry a
  # `property_id` — never a `client_id` — so a job created either way
  # otherwise saves with `client_id: nil`. That breaks anything reading
  # the client straight off the job rather than through its property
  # (story 836's invoicing does both a card-on-file charge lookup and
  # the invoice's own client label this way), so every job creation
  # backfills `client_id` from its property here rather than requiring
  # every caller to remember to. A caller that already supplies a
  # `client_id` (fixtures with only a client on hand, no property) is
  # left alone.
  defp derive_client_id(account_id, attrs) do
    if blank?(fetch_attr(attrs, :client_id)) do
      case fetch_attr(attrs, :property_id) do
        value when value in [nil, ""] -> attrs
        property_id -> put_client_id_from_property(attrs, account_id, property_id)
      end
    else
      attrs
    end
  end

  defp put_client_id_from_property(attrs, account_id, property_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Property, id: property_id, account_id: account_id) do
      %Property{client_id: client_id} when not is_nil(client_id) ->
        # Match whichever key style (atom or string) `attrs` already
        # uses — `Ecto.Changeset.cast/4` raises on a map mixing both.
        if Map.has_key?(attrs, :property_id) do
          Map.put(attrs, :client_id, client_id)
        else
          Map.put(attrs, "client_id", client_id)
        end

      _ ->
        attrs
    end
  end

  defp fetch_attr(attrs, key), do: Map.get(attrs, key) || Map.get(attrs, to_string(key))

  defp blank?(nil), do: true
  defp blank?(""), do: true
  defp blank?(_value), do: false

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :system) do
    Recorder.record_system(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :user) do
    Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  # Deliberately omits `scheduled_date`: a "created" entry's own
  # subject label (job → property/client) is enough to identify which
  # job this is, and surfacing it here would read as a schedule change
  # (`field_changes/1`'s "Scheduled date: ..." line) indistinguishable
  # from an actual reschedule recorded later by `update_job/3`.
  defp job_created_values(job) do
    %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id}
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
  """
  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.

  `:include_cancelled_ids` (default `[]`) admits specific cancelled
  jobs back in anyway — the board's own escape hatch for a cancelled
  job that still carries an unacknowledged schedule-change
  notification (story 843): the office needs to keep seeing its
  ack-status until the cleaner acknowledges, and the escalation check
  needs the job rendered at all to ever run. Other callers passing no
  opts see the same non-cancelled set as before.
  """
  def list_jobs(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    include_cancelled_ids = Keyword.get(opts, :include_cancelled_ids, [])

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and
        (j.status != :cancelled or j.id in ^include_cancelled_ids)
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
  """
  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <-
           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
             scope,
             cleaner_id,
             job.scheduled_date,
             job.start_time,
             job.end_time,
             exclude_job_id: job.id
           ),
         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_reassigned",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_cancelled",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Updates a job's schedule and/or price — a reschedule, a price
  change, or both, made directly from the board rather than through
  `assign_cleaner/3`'s conflict-checked path. Records only the fields
  that actually changed to the audit trail, attributed to the caller.
  """
  def update_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    changeset = Job.changeset(job, derive_client_id(account_id, attrs))

    with {:ok, updated} <- Repo.update(changeset) do
      record_job_updated(scope, job, changeset, updated)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @audited_update_fields ~w(scheduled_date start_time end_time agreed_price_cents status)a

  defp record_job_updated(scope, job, changeset, updated) do
    changed_fields =
      changeset.changes
      |> Map.keys()
      |> Enum.filter(&(&1 in @audited_update_fields))

    if changed_fields != [] do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        update_action(changed_fields),
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        audit_snapshot(job, changed_fields),
        audit_snapshot(updated, changed_fields)
      )
    end
  end

  defp update_action(changed_fields) do
    cond do
      Enum.any?(changed_fields, &(&1 in [:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])) ->
        "job_rescheduled"

      :agreed_price_cents in changed_fields ->
        "job_price_changed"

      true ->
        "job_updated"
    end
  end

  defp audit_snapshot(job, fields),
    do: Map.new(fields, &{to_string(&1), audit_value(Map.get(job, &1))})

  defp audit_value(%Date{} = value), do: to_string(value)
  defp audit_value(%Time{} = value), do: to_string(value)
  defp audit_value(value), do: value

  @doc """
  Removes a job from the board without hard-deleting its row — the
  row (and any audit entries already about it) stays resolvable for
  the trail. Distinct from `cancel_job/2`: this is the office
  correcting a mistaken entry rather than calling off an appointment,
  so it's recorded as "deleted" rather than "cancelled" and never
  notifies the assigned cleaner.
  """
  def delete_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_deleted",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  ## Recurring plans

  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    RecurringPlan
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan, Recurrence.occurrences(plan))
  end

  @doc """
  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
  """
  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, plan} <-
             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
             |> Repo.insert() do
        jobs =
          plan
          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs, actor: :system)
            job
          end)

        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  ## Availability blocks

  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
  end

  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
  end

  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
  through.
  """
  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
      {:ok, user}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Fetches a single cleaner by id, for their detail page. Draws from
  the same membership list as `list_cleaners/1`, so a user who isn't
  a member of this account can't be looked up here either. Raises if
  not found.
  """
  def get_cleaner!(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    cleaner_id = parse_cleaner_id(id)

    scope
    |> list_cleaners()
    |> Enum.find(&(&1.id == cleaner_id))
    |> case do
      nil -> raise Ecto.NoResultsError, queryable: User
      cleaner -> cleaner
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Lists a cleaner's time-off blocks for their detail page, soonest
  first.
  """
  def list_availability_blocks(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    cleaner_id = parse_cleaner_id(cleaner_id)

    AvailabilityBlock
    |> where([b], b.account_id == ^account_id and b.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id)
    |> order_by([b], asc: b.date)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists a cleaner's upcoming (today or later, non-cancelled) jobs for
  their detail page, soonest first.
  """
  def list_upcoming_jobs_for_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    cleaner_id = parse_cleaner_id(cleaner_id)

    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and
        j.status != :cancelled and j.scheduled_date >= ^Date.utc_today()
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  defp parse_cleaner_id(id) when is_integer(id), do: id
  defp parse_cleaner_id(id) when is_binary(id), do: String.to_integer(id)

  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing do
  @moduledoc """
  Invoices generated from completed jobs and payment collection via
  card-on-file or a public payment link, with proof-of-work attached
  from `CleanerCrm.Quality` for chargeback defense.

  Per the payments-stripe ADR, an invoice's `status` only ever advances
  on a Stripe webhook confirmation: `charge_card/2` and
  `pay_via_link/2` just submit a PaymentIntent and move the invoice to
  `:charge_pending`; only `receive_webhook/1` marks it `:paid`, or
  reverts it to `:unpaid` on a decline so the owner can retry or send a
  payment link.

  Every function that isn't reached from the public `/pay/:token` or
  `/webhooks/stripe` routes is scoped to the caller's active account —
  those two have no logged-in user to scope against.

  ## Job completion integration point

  No caller generates an invoice automatically yet: job completion
  itself lives in `CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_job/2`
  (`CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.Job`, which will drive it, doesn't exist
  yet either). Once it does, the natural hook is right there — call
  `generate_for_job/2` with the now-completed job after
  `Quality.complete_job/2` succeeds.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.{Invoice, Payment, ReceiptNotifier, StripeGateway}
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  ## Invoices

  @doc "Lists the account's invoices, most recent first, for the billing queue."
  def list_invoices(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([i], desc: i.inserted_at)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_invoice!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  @doc """
  Looks up an invoice by its public payment-link token. Takes no
  `Scope` — the payer on `/pay/:token` isn't a logged-in user, so the
  token itself (unguessable, unique) is the only access control this
  lookup has.
  """
  def get_invoice_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.payment_token == ^token)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  def create_invoice(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Invoice{account_id: account_id}
    |> Invoice.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Generates the invoice for a job that's just been marked complete —
  see the moduledoc for where this gets wired in once job completion
  has a real caller.

  Returns `{:error, :no_price}` without creating an invoice, and
  without touching the database at all, when the job has no
  `agreed_price_cents` — e.g. a visit materialized from a
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan` with no price set (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence.job_attrs/1`). Job completion itself
  must still succeed in that case, so callers should let this error
  through rather than fail the completion on it. There's no dedicated
  "completed jobs missing an invoice" queue today — the office notices
  a missing invoice by comparing the schedule board's completed jobs
  against `list_invoices/1`, or avoids it entirely by pricing the job
  (or its recurring plan) before it's completed.
  """
  def generate_for_job(%Scope{}, %Job{agreed_price_cents: nil}), do: {:error, :no_price}

  def generate_for_job(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    create_invoice(scope, %{job_id: job.id, amount_cents: job.agreed_price_cents, status: :unpaid})
  end

  ## Payment collection

  @doc """
  Charges the client's card on file for the invoice's full amount.
  Refused with `{:error, :no_card_on_file}` when the client has none.
  """
  def charge_card(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        %Invoice{account_id: account_id} = invoice
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    invoice
    |> invoice_client()
    |> submit_and_finalize_charge(invoice, off_session: true, source: "card_on_file")
  end

  defp submit_and_finalize_charge(%Client{card_on_file: false}, _invoice, _opts),
    do: {:error, :no_card_on_file}

  defp submit_and_finalize_charge(%Client{} = client, invoice, opts) do
    {source, charge_opts} = Keyword.pop!(opts, :source)

    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <-
           submit_charge(invoice, payment_method_for(client), charge_opts) do

    end
  end

  public payment-link token — the `/pay/:token` page's own flow, with
  no card on file and no logged-in payer to scope against.

    end

  defp submit_charge(%Invoice{} = invoice, payment_method, opts) do
    StripeGateway.create_payment_intent(%{
      amount_cents: invoice.amount_cents,
      payment_method: payment_method,
      off_session: Keyword.get(opts, :off_session, false),
      metadata: %{invoice_id: invoice.id}
    })
  end

  # Clients doesn't yet persist a real Stripe payment-method/customer id
  # (only the `card_on_file` flag) — this placeholder stands in until a
  # SetupIntent-backed token is stored. The Test adapter ignores it
  # entirely, and the Live adapter is never exercised without one.
  defp payment_method_for(%Client{id: id}), do: "card_on_file:#{id}"

  defp finalize_charge_submission(%Invoice{} = invoice, client, intent_id, source) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, updated} <-
             invoice
             |> Invoice.changeset(%{status: :charge_pending, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id})
             |> Repo.update(),
           {:ok, _payment} <- record_payment(updated, intent_id, source, :pending) do
        {:ok, updated}
      end
    end)
    |> tap(fn
      {:ok, updated} -> send_receipt(client, updated)
      _error -> :ok
    end)
  end

  @doc """
  Generates (or reuses) an invoice's public payment-link token, so the
  owner can share `/pay/:token` with a client who has no card on file.
  """

        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        %Invoice{account_id: account_id} = invoice
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
