    |> Invoice.changeset(%{payment_token: invoice.payment_token || generate_token()})
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  defp generate_token, do: 16 |> :crypto.strong_rand_bytes() |> Base.url_encode64(padding: false)

  defp invoice_client(%Invoice{} = invoice) do
    invoice |> Repo.preload(job: :client) |> then(& &1.job.client)
  end

  defp send_receipt(%Client{email: email}, %Invoice{} = invoice) when is_binary(email) do
    ReceiptNotifier.deliver_receipt(email, invoice)
    :ok
  end

  defp send_receipt(_client, _invoice), do: :ok

  defp record_payment(%Invoice{} = invoice, intent_id, source, status) do
    %Payment{account_id: invoice.account_id, invoice_id: invoice.id}
    |> Payment.changeset(%{
      amount_cents: invoice.amount_cents,
      status: status,
      provider: "stripe",
      stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id,
      source: source
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Webhook

  @doc """
  Verifies and applies an inbound Stripe webhook request — the
  controller's only touchpoint into this context, so it never sees
  event data it can't trust.
  """
  def receive_webhook(conn) do
    with {:ok, event} <- StripeGateway.verify_webhook_event(conn) do
      apply_webhook_event(event)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.succeeded"} = event) do
    with {:ok, invoice} <- find_invoice_for_event(event) do
      transition_invoice(invoice, :paid, :succeeded)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.payment_failed"} = event) do
    with {:ok, invoice} <- find_invoice_for_event(event) do
      transition_invoice(invoice, :unpaid, :failed)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => _other}), do: {:ok, :ignored}

  defp find_invoice_for_event(%{"data" => %{"object" => object}}) do
    case object do
      %{"metadata" => %{"invoice_id" => invoice_id}} when is_binary(invoice_id) ->
        fetch_invoice(invoice_id)

      %{"id" => intent_id} when is_binary(intent_id) ->
        fetch_invoice_by_intent(intent_id)

      _ ->
        {:error, :invoice_not_found}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_invoice(invoice_id) do
    case Repo.get(Invoice, invoice_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :invoice_not_found}
      invoice -> {:ok, invoice}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_invoice_by_intent(intent_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Invoice, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :invoice_not_found}
      invoice -> {:ok, invoice}
    end
  end

  # `stripe_payment_intent_id` is left as-is on a decline (never
  # cleared) — its presence is what tells `CleanerCrmWeb.InvoiceLive.Show`
  # to offer "retry" instead of the initial "charge card" action.
  defp transition_invoice(%Invoice{} = invoice, new_status, payment_status) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, updated} <- invoice |> Invoice.changeset(%{status: new_status}) |> Repo.update() do
        update_payment_record(updated, payment_status)
        {:ok, updated}
      end
    end)
  end

  # The `Payment` submitted alongside the charge is normally still
  # `:pending` here and just gets its outcome filled in; a fixture-seeded
  # invoice (no prior `charge_card/2` call) has none, so one is created
  # for the audit trail.
  defp update_payment_record(%Invoice{} = invoice, status) do
    case Repo.get_by(Payment,
           invoice_id: invoice.id,
           stripe_payment_intent_id: invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id
         ) do
      nil -> record_payment(invoice, invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id, "webhook", status)
      payment -> payment |> Payment.changeset(%{status: status}) |> Repo.update()
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing.Invoice do
  @moduledoc """
  An invoice for a completed job.

  Per the payments-stripe ADR, `status` only ever advances on a Stripe
  webhook confirmation: charging a card or sending a payment link just
  submits a charge and moves the invoice to `:charge_pending`; only the
  webhook marks it `:paid`, and a declined charge reverts it to
  `:unpaid` so the owner can retry or fall back to a payment link.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type status :: :unpaid | :charge_pending | :paid

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          job_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          amount_cents: integer() | nil,
          status: status(),
          stripe_payment_intent_id: String.t() | nil,
          payment_token: String.t() | nil,
          job: CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job.t() | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "invoices" do
    field :amount_cents, :integer
    field :amount, :decimal, virtual: true
    field :status, Ecto.Enum, values: [:unpaid, :charge_pending, :paid], default: :unpaid
    field :stripe_payment_intent_id, :string
    field :payment_token, :string

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :job, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(job_id amount amount_cents status stripe_payment_intent_id payment_token)a

  def changeset(invoice, attrs) do
    invoice
    |> cast(attrs, @fields)
    |> validate_required([:job_id])
    |> put_amount_cents()
    # After `put_amount_cents/1`, not before — a caller supplying dollars
    # via `amount` has no `amount_cents` yet until that step runs.
    # Needed because `validate_number/3` below only runs against an
    # actual *change*, so an explicit `amount_cents: nil` (unchanged from
    # a fresh `%Invoice{}`'s own default) silently skips it and would
    # otherwise reach `amount_cents`'s NOT NULL column as a raised
    # constraint violation instead of a changeset error.
    |> validate_required([:amount_cents])
    |> validate_number(:amount_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> unique_constraint(:payment_token)
  end

  # `amount` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the money-handling
  # ADR); rounded half-up and stored as `amount_cents` — the only column
  # ever persisted. Callers that already have cents (e.g. copying a job's
  # `agreed_price_cents`) pass `amount_cents` directly and skip this.
  defp put_amount_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :amount) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :amount_cents, cents)
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications do
  @moduledoc """
  Client appointment reminders with confirm/reschedule actions, and
  cleaner schedule-change alerts requiring explicit acknowledgment with
  office visibility into what's still unacknowledged. Email/SMS
  delivery is abstracted behind `CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery`.

  Most functions are scoped by the caller's `Scope`. The confirm,
  reschedule, and delivery-status webhook endpoints are reached by an
  unauthenticated client or provider, so they look a notification up by
  its opaque `token` (or the provider's message id) instead.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications.{
    Notification,
    ReminderNotifier,
    ReminderScheduler,
    ReminderSettings
  }

  ## Reminder settings

  @doc "The account's reminder settings, defaulting to a 24-hour lead time if never configured."
  def get_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(ReminderSettings, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> %ReminderSettings{account_id: account_id}
      settings -> settings
    end
  end

  def change_reminder_settings(%Scope{} = scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope |> get_reminder_settings() |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
  end

  def update_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> get_reminder_settings()
    |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()

  @doc "The office's delivery log: every notification for the account, most recent first."
  def list_notifications(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do

    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> preload([:client, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.all()

  ## Public confirm/reschedule — reached by token, no scope available

  def get_notification_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do

  def confirm_reminder(token) when is_binary(token) do

    else

    end

  def request_reschedule(token) when is_binary(token) do

        status: :reschedule_requested,
        reschedule_requested_at: DateTime.utc_now()

  @doc "True once the client has confirmed the most recent reminder sent for this job."
  def job_confirmed?(job_id) do

    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :confirmed)

  acknowledged (`:pending` or `:escalated`) — for `ScheduleLive.Index`
  to keep a cancelled job's row (and its ack-status/channel
  indicators) on the board until the office has visibility into it,
  per story 843's escalation path. A job with no schedule-change
  notification at all, or whose latest one is already `:acknowledged`,
  is left out.

  def job_ids_with_unacknowledged_schedule_change(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.account_id == ^account_id and n.kind == :schedule_change)
    |> distinct([n], n.job_id)
    |> order_by([n], asc: n.job_id, desc: n.inserted_at)

  The most recent schedule-change alert pushed for this job — `nil`,
  or a `Notification` exposing `:status`
  (`:pending` | `:acknowledged` | `:escalated`) and `:channel`
  (`:push` | `:sms` | `:email`). This is the contract
  `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.Index` reads defensively to show a job's
  ack status on the board.
  """
  def latest_schedule_change_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, job_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where(
      [n],
      n.account_id == ^account_id and n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :schedule_change
    )
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
    |> maybe_escalate()
  end

  # A same-day change nobody has acknowledged within the escalation
  # window re-sends via the fallback channel (SMS) and flags as
  # escalated for office visibility. Computed on read rather than a
  # separate periodic pass — every read of a job's alert (the board,
  # `FieldLive.Today`) goes through here, so none of them can show a
  # stale "pending" past the window.

    if escalation_due?(notification) do
      {:ok, updated} =
        update_status(notification,
          status: :escalated,
          channel: :sms,
          escalated_at: DateTime.utc_now()
        )

    else
      notification
    end
  end

  defp maybe_escalate(notification), do: notification

  defp escalation_due?(%Notification{pushed_at: nil}), do: false

  defp escalation_due?(%Notification{pushed_at: pushed_at, job_id: job_id}) do
    job = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, job_id)

    Date.compare(job.scheduled_date, Date.utc_today()) != :gt and
      DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(), pushed_at, :second) >= @escalation_window_seconds
  end

  ## Shared helpers

  @doc false
  def generate_token, do: Base.url_encode64(:crypto.strong_rand_bytes(24), padding: false)

  defp update_status(%Notification{} = notification, attrs) do
    notification
    |> Notification.changeset(Map.new(attrs))
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  # exception for building absolute links in outbound messages — see
  # the `dirty_xrefs` note on the `CleanerCrm` boundary.
  defp reminder_url(path), do: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> path

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.Today do @moduledoc """ The cleaner's day view: today's (or a looked-ahead day's) jobs in start-time order, each carrying everything needed to get in the door, plus any pending schedule-change alerts and the current pay-period earnings summary. Route: `/field`, with an optional `?date=` query param to look ahead at a future day. Lockbox/alarm codes unmask only once the real calendar date reaches a job's own scheduled date — never earlier, regardless of which day is currently being browsed. ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Scheduling` — the account's jobs, filtered here to this cleaner's own jobs for the selected day. - `CleanerCrm.Notifications` — read defensively (`Code.ensure_loaded?/1` + `function_exported?/3`): it may land after this view does, and this view must never crash for its absence. - `CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.EarningsComponent` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling alias CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.EarningsComponent @impl true def render(assigns) do ~H"""
<.header> {Calendar.strftime(@date, "%A, %B %-d")} <:subtitle>{length(@jobs)} job{if length(@jobs) == 1, do: "", else: "s"} today

Schedule change

{notification.change_summary}

<.live_component module={EarningsComponent} id="pay-period-earnings" current_scope={@current_scope} />

No jobs scheduled for this day.

{format_time(job.start_time)} <.link navigate={~p"/field/jobs/#{job.id}"} class="link link-primary text-sm"> Open job
{address(job)}
Entry:
{detail(job, :entry_method, "No entry method on file")}
Parking:
{detail(job, :parking_notes, "No parking notes")}
Pets:
{detail(job, :pet_notes, "No pet notes on file")}
Preferences:
{detail(job, :client_preferences, "No client preferences on file")}
<.access_codes job={job} />
""" end attr :job, :map, required: true defp access_codes(assigns) do ~H"""
Lockbox: {mask_or_reveal(@job, @job.property.lockbox_code)}
Alarm: {mask_or_reveal(@job, @job.property.alarm_code)}

Unlocks on the day of the job

defmodule CleanerCrm.TimeTracking do
  @moduledoc """
  Clock-in/out per job, hourly and piece-rate pay, transparent
  per-job and pay-period earnings, and payroll-ready CSV export.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account. Money is
  always integer cents; `CleanerCrm.Money` formats it for display and
  `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings` does the cents math.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.{Earnings, PayRate, PayrollExport, TimeEntry}
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.{Scope, User}

  ## Clocking in and out

  @doc """
  Clocks the scope's user in to `job`. Fails closed: `{:error,
  :not_assigned}` if the job isn't theirs, `{:error,
  {:already_clocked_in, other_job}}` if they're still on the clock
  somewhere else.
  """
  def clock_in(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <- ensure_assigned(job, scope.user),
         :ok <- ensure_not_already_clocked_in(scope, job) do
      create_time_entry(scope, %{job_id: job.id, clocked_in_at: DateTime.utc_now()})
    end
  end

  @doc "Clocks the scope's user out of their open entry on `job`."
  def clock_out(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job) do
      nil ->
        {:error, :not_clocked_in}

      entry ->
        entry |> TimeEntry.changeset(%{clocked_out_at: DateTime.utc_now()}) |> Repo.update()
    end
  end

  defp ensure_assigned(%Job{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}, %User{id: cleaner_id}), do: :ok
  defp ensure_assigned(_job, _user), do: {:error, :not_assigned}

  defp ensure_not_already_clocked_in(%Scope{user: user} = scope, %Job{id: job_id}) do
    case open_time_entry_for_cleaner(scope, user.id) do
      nil -> :ok
      %TimeEntry{job_id: ^job_id} -> :ok
      %TimeEntry{} = entry -> {:error, {:already_clocked_in, Repo.preload(entry, :job).job}}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a resolved (or open, if `clocked_out_at` is omitted or
  `nil`) time entry directly. The sanctioned bypass
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.time_entry_fixture` seeds through — real
  clock-in/out goes through `clock_in/2` and `clock_out/2` above.
  """
  def create_time_entry(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, fetch!(attrs, :job_id))

    %TimeEntry{account_id: account_id, job_id: job.id, cleaner_id: job.cleaner_id}
    |> TimeEntry.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Sets the clock-out time on an open entry to a specific time of day
  on its clock-in date — how the owner resolves a forgotten
  clock-out.
  """
  def resolve_clock_out(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %TimeEntry{} = entry, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, time} <- parse_time(fetch!(attrs, :clock_out_time)),
         {:ok, clocked_out_at} <- combine(entry.clocked_in_at, time) do
      entry |> TimeEntry.changeset(%{clocked_out_at: clocked_out_at}) |> Repo.update()
    end
  end

  defp fetch!(attrs, key) do
    case Map.fetch(attrs, key) do
      {:ok, value} -> value
      :error -> Map.fetch!(attrs, to_string(key))
    end
  end

  defp parse_time(%Time{} = time), do: {:ok, time}

  defp parse_time(string) when is_binary(string) do
    case String.split(string, ":") do
      [_hour, _minute] -> Time.from_iso8601(string <> ":00")
      _ -> Time.from_iso8601(string)
    end
  end

  # Combines the submitted time-of-day with the clock-in's date. A
  # resolution submitted for the same day is the common case, but a
  # cleaner who clocked in late at night and got resolved the next
  # morning would otherwise land before their own clock-in and fail
  # validation — so a candidate that doesn't come after clock-in rolls
  # forward to the next day instead.
  defp combine(%DateTime{time_zone: time_zone} = clocked_in_at, %Time{} = time) do
    date = DateTime.to_date(clocked_in_at)

    with {:ok, candidate} <- DateTime.new(date, time, time_zone) do
      if DateTime.compare(candidate, clocked_in_at) == :gt do
        {:ok, candidate}
      else
        DateTime.new(Date.add(date, 1), time, time_zone)
      end
    end
  end

  ## Reading time entries

  def open_time_entry_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.job_id == ^job.id and is_nil(t.clocked_out_at)
    )
    |> order_by([t], desc: t.clocked_in_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  def open_time_entry_for_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and is_nil(t.clocked_out_at)
    )
    |> order_by([t], desc: t.clocked_in_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  def list_time_entries_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id and t.job_id == ^job.id)
    |> order_by([t], asc: t.clocked_in_at)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Earnings

  @doc """
  Cents earned on `job` so far — see `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings.job_cents/2`
  for exactly what that means for each pay type.
  """
  def job_earnings_cents(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    Earnings.job_cents(job, list_time_entries_for_job(scope, job))
  end

  @doc "Seconds elapsed on the cleaner's currently-open entry for `job`, or `nil` if not clocked in."
  def elapsed_seconds(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    case open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job) do
      nil -> nil
      entry -> Earnings.elapsed_seconds(entry)
    end
  end

  ## Pay periods

  @doc "The Monday-Sunday week containing `date`."
  def pay_period_for(%Date{} = date) do
    monday = Date.add(date, -(Date.day_of_week(date) - 1))
    {monday, Date.add(monday, 6)}
  end

  @doc """
  The account's current pay period: the week containing its most
  recent time entry, falling back to this real-world week when the
  account has none yet. Anchoring on the latest activity rather than
  the wall clock means newly-seeded or backfilled data is visible the
  moment the owner opens the timesheet, with no period picker to
  navigate first.
  """
  def current_pay_period(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> select([t], max(t.clocked_in_at))
    |> Repo.one()
    |> case do
      nil -> Date.utc_today()
      clocked_in_at -> DateTime.to_date(clocked_in_at)
    end
    |> pay_period_for()
  end

  @doc """
  Every job with time recorded in `period` (a `{start_date, end_date}`
  tuple), with its cleaner, entries, earned cents (`nil` if
  unresolved), and resolved status — the timesheet's row-level data.
  """
  def list_job_time_summaries(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, {_, _} = period)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> time_entries_in_period(period)
    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.job_id)
    |> Enum.map(fn {_job_id, entries} ->
      job = hd(entries).job
      cents = Earnings.job_cents(job, entries)
      open? = Enum.any?(entries, &(!TimeEntry.resolved?(&1)))

      %{
        job: job,
        cleaner: job.cleaner,
        entries: entries,
        cents: cents,
        # `open?` is genuinely missing a clock-out — the only state a
        # clock-out resolution can fix. `unresolved?` is broader: it
        # also covers a job whose entries are all closed but whose pay
        # can't be computed yet (missing pay type/rate), which must
        # block payroll the same way an open entry does rather than
        # silently price at $0 — but has no open entry for a
        # clock-out resolution to act on, so the two are tracked
        # separately rather than folded into one flag.
        open?: open?,
        unresolved?: is_nil(cents) or open?
      }
    end)
    |> Enum.sort_by(& &1.job.scheduled_date, Date)
  end

  @doc """
  Per-cleaner totals for `period`, excluding unresolved jobs. A
  cleaner whose only job is unresolved still appears, at zero — the
  amount isn't missing, it's withheld pending resolution.
  """
  def cleaner_pay_totals(%Scope{} = scope, period) do
    scope
    |> list_job_time_summaries(period)
    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.cleaner.id)
    |> Map.new(fn {cleaner_id, summaries} ->
      total = summaries |> Enum.reject(& &1.unresolved?) |> Enum.map(& &1.cents) |> Enum.sum()
      {cleaner_id, total}
    end)
  end

  defp time_entries_in_period(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, {start_date, end_date}) do
    start_at = DateTime.new!(start_date, ~T[00:00:00])
    end_at = DateTime.new!(Date.add(end_date, 1), ~T[00:00:00])

    TimeEntry
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.clocked_in_at >= ^start_at and t.clocked_in_at < ^end_at
    )
    |> preload(job: :cleaner)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Payroll export

  @doc """
  Exports `period`'s earnings to CSV, one row per cleaner. Refuses
  with `{:error, :unresolved_entries}` while any job in the period is
  still missing a clock-out — payroll never goes out on an estimate.
  """
  def export_pay_period_csv(%Scope{} = scope, period) do
    summaries = list_job_time_summaries(scope, period)

    if Enum.any?(summaries, & &1.unresolved?) do
      {:error, :unresolved_entries}
    else
      {:ok, PayrollExport.to_csv(summaries)}
    end
  end

  ## Drive-time policy

  @doc "The account's drive-time pay policy, for display alongside a cleaner's earnings."
  def drive_time_policy(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Accounts.get_account!(scope, account_id).drive_time_policy
  end

  ## Pay rates (per-cleaner defaults)

  def get_pay_rate(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.get_by(PayRate, account_id: account_id, cleaner_id: cleaner_id)
  end

  def set_pay_rate(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, cleaner_id, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> get_pay_rate(cleaner_id)
    |> Kernel.||(%PayRate{account_id: account_id, cleaner_id: cleaner_id})
    |> PayRate.changeset(Map.put(attrs, :cleaner_id, cleaner_id))
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
  end
end

    %TimeEntry{account_id: account_id, job_id: job.id, cleaner_id: job.cleaner_id}
    |> TimeEntry.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Sets the clock-out time on an open entry to a specific time of day
  on its clock-in date — how the owner resolves a forgotten
  clock-out.
  """
  def resolve_clock_out(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %TimeEntry{} = entry, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, time} <- parse_time(fetch!(attrs, :clock_out_time)),
         {:ok, clocked_out_at} <- combine(entry.clocked_in_at, time) do
      entry |> TimeEntry.changeset(%{clocked_out_at: clocked_out_at}) |> Repo.update()
    end
  end

  defp fetch!(attrs, key) do
    case Map.fetch(attrs, key) do
      {:ok, value} -> value
      :error -> Map.fetch!(attrs, to_string(key))
    end
  end

  defp parse_time(%Time{} = time), do: {:ok, time}

  defp parse_time(string) when is_binary(string) do
    case String.split(string, ":") do
      [_hour, _minute] -> Time.from_iso8601(string <> ":00")
      _ -> Time.from_iso8601(string)
    end
  end

  # Combines the submitted time-of-day with the clock-in's date. A
  # resolution submitted for the same day is the common case, but a
  # cleaner who clocked in late at night and got resolved the next
  # morning would otherwise land before their own clock-in and fail
  # validation — so a candidate that doesn't come after clock-in rolls
  # forward to the next day instead.
  defp combine(%DateTime{time_zone: time_zone} = clocked_in_at, %Time{} = time) do
    date = DateTime.to_date(clocked_in_at)

    with {:ok, candidate} <- DateTime.new(date, time, time_zone) do
      if DateTime.compare(candidate, clocked_in_at) == :gt do
        {:ok, candidate}
      else
        DateTime.new(Date.add(date, 1), time, time_zone)
      end
    end
  end

  ## Reading time entries

  def open_time_entry_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.job_id == ^job.id and is_nil(t.clocked_out_at)
    )
    |> order_by([t], desc: t.clocked_in_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  def open_time_entry_for_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and is_nil(t.clocked_out_at)
    )
    |> order_by([t], desc: t.clocked_in_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  def list_time_entries_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id and t.job_id == ^job.id)
    |> order_by([t], asc: t.clocked_in_at)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Earnings

  @doc """
  Cents earned on `job` so far — see `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings.job_cents/2`
  for exactly what that means for each pay type.
  """
  def job_earnings_cents(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    Earnings.job_cents(job, list_time_entries_for_job(scope, job))
  end

  @doc "Seconds elapsed on the cleaner's currently-open entry for `job`, or `nil` if not clocked in."
  def elapsed_seconds(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    case open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job) do
      nil -> nil
      entry -> Earnings.elapsed_seconds(entry)
    end
  end

  ## Pay periods

  @doc "The Monday-Sunday week containing `date`."
  def pay_period_for(%Date{} = date) do
    monday = Date.add(date, -(Date.day_of_week(date) - 1))
    {monday, Date.add(monday, 6)}
  end

  @doc """
  The account's current pay period: the week containing its most
  recent time entry, falling back to this real-world week when the
  account has none yet. Anchoring on the latest activity rather than
  the wall clock means newly-seeded or backfilled data is visible the
  moment the owner opens the timesheet, with no period picker to
  navigate first.
  """
  def current_pay_period(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> select([t], max(t.clocked_in_at))
    |> Repo.one()
    |> case do
      nil -> Date.utc_today()
      clocked_in_at -> DateTime.to_date(clocked_in_at)
    end
    |> pay_period_for()
  end

  @doc """
  Every job with time recorded in `period` (a `{start_date, end_date}`
  tuple), with its cleaner, entries, earned cents (`nil` if
  unresolved), and resolved status — the timesheet's row-level data.
  """
  def list_job_time_summaries(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, {_, _} = period)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> time_entries_in_period(period)
    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.job_id)
    |> Enum.map(fn {_job_id, entries} ->
      job = hd(entries).job
      cents = Earnings.job_cents(job, entries)
      open? = Enum.any?(entries, &(!TimeEntry.resolved?(&1)))

      %{
        job: job,
        cleaner: job.cleaner,
        entries: entries,
        cents: cents,
        # `open?` is genuinely missing a clock-out — the only state a
        # clock-out resolution can fix. `unresolved?` is broader: it
        # also covers a job whose entries are all closed but whose pay
        # can't be computed yet (missing pay type/rate), which must
        # block payroll the same way an open entry does rather than
        # silently price at $0 — but has no open entry for a
        # clock-out resolution to act on, so the two are tracked
        # separately rather than folded into one flag.
        open?: open?,
        unresolved?: is_nil(cents) or open?
      }
    end)
    |> Enum.sort_by(& &1.job.scheduled_date, Date)
  end

  @doc """
  Per-cleaner totals for `period`, excluding unresolved jobs. A
  cleaner whose only job is unresolved still appears, at zero — the
  amount isn't missing, it's withheld pending resolution.
  """
  def cleaner_pay_totals(%Scope{} = scope, period) do
    scope
    |> list_job_time_summaries(period)
    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.cleaner.id)
    |> Map.new(fn {cleaner_id, summaries} ->
      total = summaries |> Enum.reject(& &1.unresolved?) |> Enum.map(& &1.cents) |> Enum.sum()
      {cleaner_id, total}
    end)
  end

  defp time_entries_in_period(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, {start_date, end_date}) do
    start_at = DateTime.new!(start_date, ~T[00:00:00])
    end_at = DateTime.new!(Date.add(end_date, 1), ~T[00:00:00])

    TimeEntry
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.clocked_in_at >= ^start_at and t.clocked_in_at < ^end_at
    )
    |> preload(job: :cleaner)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Payroll export

  @doc """
  Exports `period`'s earnings to CSV, one row per cleaner. Refuses
  with `{:error, :unresolved_entries}` while any job in the period is
  still missing a clock-out — payroll never goes out on an estimate.
  """
  def export_pay_period_csv(%Scope{} = scope, period) do
    summaries = list_job_time_summaries(scope, period)

    if Enum.any?(summaries, & &1.unresolved?) do
      {:error, :unresolved_entries}
    else
      {:ok, PayrollExport.to_csv(summaries)}
    end
  end

  ## Drive-time policy

  @doc "The account's drive-time pay policy, for display alongside a cleaner's earnings."
  def drive_time_policy(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Accounts.get_account!(scope, account_id).drive_time_policy
  end

  ## Pay rates (per-cleaner defaults)

  def get_pay_rate(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.get_by(PayRate, account_id: account_id, cleaner_id: cleaner_id)
  end

  def set_pay_rate(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, cleaner_id, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> get_pay_rate(cleaner_id)
    |> Kernel.||(%PayRate{account_id: account_id, cleaner_id: cleaner_id})
    |> PayRate.changeset(Map.put(attrs, :cleaner_id, cleaner_id))
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings do
  @moduledoc """
  Pure pay calculations — no scope, no `Repo`. Given a job and its
  time entries, this is the only place clocked time (or a fixed piece
  rate) turns into cents.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.TimeEntry

  @doc "Seconds between clock-in and clock-out. Only meaningful once resolved."
  def worked_seconds(%TimeEntry{clocked_in_at: in_at, clocked_out_at: out_at})
      when not is_nil(out_at) do
    DateTime.diff(out_at, in_at, :second)
  end

  @doc "Seconds elapsed so far on a still-open entry."
  def elapsed_seconds(%TimeEntry{clocked_out_at: nil, clocked_in_at: in_at}) do
    DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(), in_at, :second)
  end

  @doc """
  Cents earned on a job given its (possibly empty) list of time
  entries: the flat piece rate regardless of time for a piece-rate job
  — shown even before the cleaner has started, since it doesn't
  depend on any entry existing — or the hourly rate times total
  resolved worked time. `nil` when an hourly job has no resolved
  entries yet, or a job carries neither pay type: there's nothing to
  compute pay from, and it must not be silently priced at $0.
  """
  def job_cents(%Job{pay_type: :piece_rate, piece_rate_cents: cents}, _entries)
      when is_integer(cents) do
    cents
  end

  def job_cents(%Job{pay_type: :hourly, hourly_rate_cents: rate}, entries)
      when is_integer(rate) and is_list(entries) and entries != [] do
    if Enum.all?(entries, &TimeEntry.resolved?/1) do
      entries |> Enum.map(&worked_seconds/1) |> Enum.sum() |> hourly_cents(rate)
    end
  end

  def job_cents(_job, _entries), do: nil

  defp hourly_cents(seconds, rate_cents) do
    Decimal.new(rate_cents)
    |> Decimal.mult(Decimal.div(Decimal.new(seconds), Decimal.new(3600)))
    |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up)
    |> Decimal.to_integer()
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

  import Plug.Conn
  import Phoenix.Controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  # Make the remember me cookie valid for 14 days. This should match
  # the session validity setting in UserToken.
  @max_cookie_age_in_days 14
  @remember_me_cookie "_cleaner_crm_web_user_remember_me"
  @remember_me_options [
    sign: true,
    max_age: @max_cookie_age_in_days * 24 * 60 * 60,
    same_site: "Lax"
  ]

  # How old the session token should be before a new one is issued. When a request is made
  # with a session token older than this value, then a new session token will be created
  # and the session and remember-me cookies (if set) will be updated with the new token.
  # Lowering this value will result in more tokens being created by active users. Increasing
  # it will result in less time before a session token expires for a user to get issued a new
  # token. This can be set to a value greater than `@max_cookie_age_in_days` to disable
  # the reissuing of tokens completely.
  @session_reissue_age_in_days 7

  @doc """
  Logs the user in.

  Redirects to the session's `:user_return_to` path
  or falls back to the `signed_in_path/1`.
  """
  def log_in_user(conn, user, params \\ %{}) do
    user_return_to = get_session(conn, :user_return_to)

    conn
    |> create_or_extend_session(user, params)
    |> redirect(to: user_return_to || signed_in_path(conn))
  end

  @doc """
  Logs the user out.

  It clears all session data for safety. See renew_session.
  """
  def log_out_user(conn) do
    user_token = get_session(conn, :user_token)
    user_token && Users.delete_user_session_token(user_token)

    if live_socket_id = get_session(conn, :live_socket_id) do
      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.broadcast(live_socket_id, "disconnect", %{})
    end

    conn
    |> renew_session(nil)
    |> delete_resp_cookie(@remember_me_cookie, @remember_me_options)
    |> redirect(to: ~p"/")
  end

  @doc """
  Authenticates the user by looking into the session and remember me token.

  Will reissue the session token if it is older than the configured age.
  """
  def fetch_current_scope_for_user(conn, _opts) do
    with {token, conn} <- ensure_user_token(conn),
         {user, token_inserted_at} <- Users.get_user_by_session_token(token) do
      conn
      |> assign(:current_scope, scope_with_active_account(user))
      |> maybe_reissue_user_session_token(user, token_inserted_at)
    else
      nil -> assign(conn, :current_scope, Scope.for_user(nil))
    end
  end

  defp ensure_user_token(conn) do
    if token = get_session(conn, :user_token) do
      {token, conn}
    else
      conn = fetch_cookies(conn, signed: [@remember_me_cookie])

      if token = conn.cookies[@remember_me_cookie] do
        {token, conn |> put_token_in_session(token) |> put_session(:user_remember_me, true)}
      else
        nil
      end
    end
  end

  # Reissue the session token if it is older than the configured reissue age.
  defp maybe_reissue_user_session_token(conn, user, token_inserted_at) do
    token_age = DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(:second), token_inserted_at, :day)

    if token_age >= @session_reissue_age_in_days do
      create_or_extend_session(conn, user, %{})
    else
      conn
    end
  end

  # This function is the one responsible for creating session tokens
  # and storing them safely in the session and cookies. It may be called
  # either when logging in, during sudo mode, or to renew a session which
  # will soon expire.
  #
  # When the session is created, rather than extended, the renew_session
  # function will clear the session to avoid fixation attacks. See the
  # renew_session function to customize this behaviour.
  defp create_or_extend_session(conn, user, params) do
    token = Users.generate_user_session_token(user)
    remember_me = get_session(conn, :user_remember_me)

    conn
    |> renew_session(user)
    |> put_token_in_session(token)
    |> maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(token, params, remember_me)
  end

  # Do not renew session if the user is already logged in
  # to prevent CSRF errors or data being lost in tabs that are still open
  defp renew_session(conn, user) when conn.assigns.current_scope.user.id == user.id do
    conn
  end

  # This function renews the session ID and erases the whole
  # session to avoid fixation attacks. If there is any data
  # in the session you may want to preserve after log in/log out,
  # you must explicitly fetch the session data before clearing
  # and then immediately set it after clearing, for example:
  #
  #     defp renew_session(conn, _user) do
  #       delete_csrf_token()
  #       preferred_locale = get_session(conn, :preferred_locale)
  #
  #       conn
  #       |> configure_session(renew: true)
  #       |> clear_session()
  #       |> put_session(:preferred_locale, preferred_locale)
  #     end
  #
  defp renew_session(conn, _user) do
    delete_csrf_token()

    conn
    |> configure_session(renew: true)
    |> clear_session()
  end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole do
  @moduledoc """
  Restricts office-only surfaces — scheduling, timesheets (including
  the payroll CSV export), quality, invoices, clients, quotes,
  reminders, and the audit trail — to account owners and admins.

  A cleaner (or anyone with no office role on the active account) is
  redirected to `/field`, their own surface, with an error flash.

  ## Usage

  As a LiveView `on_mount` hook, listed after
  `CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth`'s `:require_authenticated` in the same
  `live_session` (it relies on `current_scope.user` already being
  assigned):

      live_session :require_office_role,
        on_mount: [
          {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
          {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
        ] do
        live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
        ...
      end

  As a plug, listed after `:require_authenticated_user` in the
  pipeline, for controller routes such as the timesheet CSV export:

      pipeline :require_office_role do
        plug CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole
      end
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

  import Plug.Conn
  import Phoenix.Controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts

  @behaviour Plug

  @impl Plug
  def init(opts), do: opts

  @impl Plug
  def call(conn, _opts) do
    if office_role?(conn.assigns.current_scope) do
      conn
    else
      conn
      |> put_flash(:error, "You don't have access to that page.")
      |> redirect(to: ~p"/field")
      |> halt()
    end
  end

  def on_mount(:default, _params, _session, socket) do
    scope = socket.assigns.current_scope

    if office_role?(scope) do
      {:cont, socket}
    else
      socket =
        socket
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "You don't have access to that page.")
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/field")

      {:halt, socket}
    end
  end

  defp office_role?(%{active_account_id: nil}), do: false

  defp office_role?(scope),
    do: Accounts.get_user_role(scope, scope.user.id, scope.active_account_id) in [:owner, :admin]
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PaymentController do
  @moduledoc """
  Public payment-link pages: a client without a card on file reaches
  `/pay/:token` (the link `CleanerCrmWeb.InvoiceLive.Show` sends) to
  pay an invoice directly, no login required.

  ## Dependencies

  - `CleanerCrm.Billing`
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing

  def show(conn, %{"token" => token}) do
    case Billing.get_invoice_by_token(token) do
      nil -> render_not_found(conn)
      invoice -> render(conn, :show, invoice: invoice)
    end
  end

  def create(conn, %{"token" => token} = params) do
    case Billing.get_invoice_by_token(token) do
      nil -> render_not_found(conn)
      invoice -> submit_payment(conn, invoice, params)
    end
  end

  defp submit_payment(conn, invoice, params) do
    payment_method = Map.get(params, "payment_method")
    save_card = Map.get(params, "save_card") in ["true", "on"]

    case Billing.pay_via_link(invoice, payment_method) do
      {:ok, updated} ->
        render(conn, :paid, invoice: updated, save_card: save_card)

      {:error, reason} ->
        render(conn, :declined, invoice: invoice, message: decline_message(reason))
    end
  end

  # A genuine card decline gets its own message; anything else (a
  # misconfigured or unreachable payment provider) gets a neutral one —
  # never blaming the payer's card for what's actually our problem.
  defp decline_message(%{"code" => "card_declined"}) do
    "Your card was declined. Please try a different payment method or contact us for help."
  end

  defp decline_message(_reason) do
    "We couldn't process your payment right now. Please try again shortly or contact us for help."
  end

  defp render_not_found(conn) do
    conn
    |> put_status(:not_found)
    |> render(:not_found)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway do
  @moduledoc """
  Hides the Stripe API behind two operations: submitting a charge as a
  PaymentIntent, and verifying an inbound webhook request. `CleanerCrm.Billing`
  calls through the configured adapter — `Test` in test (see
  `config/test.exs`), `Live` everywhere else — so a test never reaches
  the real Stripe API, and the real adapter is the only one that ever
  checks a webhook signature.

  Configure the adapter and (for `Live`) credentials with:

      config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway,
        adapter: CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Live,
        secret_key: System.get_env("STRIPE_SECRET_KEY"),
        webhook_secret: System.get_env("STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET")
  """

  @type charge_params :: %{
          required(:amount_cents) => pos_integer(),
          required(:payment_method) => String.t(),
          optional(:off_session) => boolean(),
          optional(:metadata) => map()
        }

  @callback create_payment_intent(charge_params()) ::
              {:ok, %{id: String.t(), status: String.t()}} | {:error, map()}

  @callback verify_webhook_event(Plug.Conn.t()) :: {:ok, map()} | {:error, atom()}

  def create_payment_intent(params), do: adapter().create_payment_intent(params)

  def verify_webhook_event(conn), do: adapter().verify_webhook_event(conn)

  defp adapter do
    :cleaner_crm
    |> Application.get_env(__MODULE__, [])
    |> Keyword.get(:adapter, __MODULE__.Live)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Users.Scope do
  @moduledoc """
  Defines the scope of the caller to be used throughout the app.

  The `CleanerCrm.Users.Scope` allows public interfaces to receive
  information about the caller, such as if the call is initiated from an
  end-user, and if so, which user. Additionally, such a scope can carry fields
  such as "super user" or other privileges for use in authorization checks,
  or to ensure specific code paths can only be accessed for a given scope.

  It is useful for logging as well as for scoping pubsub subscriptions and
  broadcasts when a caller subscribes to an interface or performs a particular
  action.

  Feel free to extend the fields on this struct to fit the needs of
  growing application requirements.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  defstruct user: nil,
            active_account: nil,
            active_account_id: nil

  @doc """
  Creates a scope for the given user.

  Returns nil if no user is given.
  """
  def for_user(%User{} = user) do
    %__MODULE__{user: user}
  end

  def for_user(nil), do: nil
end

1	defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.ScheduleNotifier do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Composes the cleaner-facing schedule-change alert (story 843) shared
4	  by every path that can reschedule, reassign, or cancel a job from the
5	  board: `ScheduleLive.Index`'s inline time/cleaner controls and cancel
6	  button, and `ScheduleLive.JobFormComponent`'s "Edit Job" dialog.
7	
8	  This is the sanctioned place for it, not `CleanerCrm.Scheduling`: the
9	  dependency graph has `Notifications -> Scheduling`, so `Scheduling`
10	  itself must never call back into `Notifications` — callers under
11	  `schedule_live/` are what's allowed to depend on both and compose
12	  them.
13	  """
14	
15	  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
16	
17	  @doc """
18	  Creates a pending schedule-change notification for `job`'s assigned
19	  cleaner. No-ops for an unassigned job (nobody to notify) or if
20	  `CleanerCrm.Notifications` isn't loaded yet.
21	  """
22	  def notify_schedule_change(scope, job, change_summary) do
23	    if job.cleaner_id && notifications_ready?(:create_notification, 2) do
24	      cleaner = Enum.find(Scheduling.list_cleaners(scope), &(&1.id == job.cleaner_id))
25	
26	      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(scope, %{
27	        cleaner_id: job.cleaner_id,
28	        job_id: job.id,
29	        kind: :schedule_change,
30	        channel: notification_channel(cleaner),
31	        status: :pending,
32	        change_summary: change_summary,
33	        pushed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
34	        token: "schedule_change_#{job.id}_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
35	      })
36	    end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.ScheduleNotifier do
  @moduledoc """
  Composes the cleaner-facing schedule-change alert (story 843) shared
  by every path that can reschedule, reassign, or cancel a job from the
  board: `ScheduleLive.Index`'s inline time/cleaner controls and cancel
  button, and `ScheduleLive.JobFormComponent`'s "Edit Job" dialog.

  This is the sanctioned place for it, not `CleanerCrm.Scheduling`: the
  dependency graph has `Notifications -> Scheduling`, so `Scheduling`
  itself must never call back into `Notifications` — callers under
  `schedule_live/` are what's allowed to depend on both and compose
  them.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling

  @doc """
  Creates a pending schedule-change notification for `job`'s assigned
  cleaner. No-ops for an unassigned job (nobody to notify) or if
  `CleanerCrm.Notifications` isn't loaded yet.
  """
  def notify_schedule_change(scope, job, change_summary) do
    if job.cleaner_id && notifications_ready?(:create_notification, 2) do
      cleaner = Enum.find(Scheduling.list_cleaners(scope), &(&1.id == job.cleaner_id))

      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(scope, %{
        cleaner_id: job.cleaner_id,
        job_id: job.id,
        kind: :schedule_change,
        channel: notification_channel(cleaner),
        status: :pending,
        change_summary: change_summary,
        pushed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
        token: "schedule_change_#{job.id}_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
      })
    end
  end

  # Falls back to SMS when the cleaner has push notifications
  # disabled. There's no such preference on `CleanerCrm.Users.User`
  # yet, so this is currently always `:push` — matched defensively so
  # it starts honoring the preference the moment that field lands,
  # with no further change needed here.
  defp notification_channel(%{push_enabled: false}), do: :sms
  defp notification_channel(_cleaner), do: :push

  @doc """
  Whether `CleanerCrm.Notifications` exports `fun/arity` — read
  defensively (`function_exported?` rather than a direct call) so
  callers tolerate that context landing or changing shape
  independently of the schedule board.
  """
  def notifications_ready?(fun, arity),
    do:
      Code.ensure_loaded?(CleanerCrm.Notifications) and
        function_exported?(CleanerCrm.Notifications, fun, arity)

  def format_time_12h(%Time{} = time) do
    {hour, period} = to_12_hour(time.hour)
    "#{hour}:#{time.minute |> Integer.to_string() |> String.pad_leading(2, "0")} #{period}"
  end

  defp to_12_hour(0), do: {12, "AM"}
  defp to_12_hour(hour) when hour < 12, do: {hour, "AM"}
  defp to_12_hour(12), do: {12, "PM"}
  defp to_12_hour(hour), do: {hour - 12, "PM"}
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Clients.Client do
  @moduledoc """
  A paying customer with contact info and preferences.

  Scoped to an account: every client belongs to exactly one account and
  is only ever visible within that account.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          name: String.t() | nil,
          active: boolean(),
          card_on_file: boolean(),
          email: String.t() | nil,
          phone: String.t() | nil,
          preferred_channel: :email | :sms,
          properties: [CleanerCrm.Clients.Property.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "clients" do
    field :name, :string
    field :active, :boolean, default: true
    field :card_on_file, :boolean, default: false
    field :email, :string
    field :phone, :string
    field :preferred_channel, Ecto.Enum, values: [:email, :sms], default: :email

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    has_many :properties, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  def changeset(client, attrs) do
    client
    |> cast(attrs, [:name, :active, :card_on_file, :email, :phone, :preferred_channel])
    |> validate_required([:name], message: "is required")
    |> validate_length(:name, min: 1, max: 200)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job do
  @moduledoc """
  A single scheduled visit: a property (or client), a time window, and
  an optional assigned cleaner.

  A job is either a one-off (`recurring_plan_id` is `nil`) or one
  occurrence materialized from a `RecurringPlan`'s cadence (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`). Both `client_id` and
  `property_id` are independently optional at the schema level — some
  callers (time tracking, quality, notifications) only ever have a
  client on hand, while the schedule board's own job form always
  carries a property.

  ## Status

  `:scheduled` (default) -> `:in_progress` -> `:completed`, or
  `:scheduled` -> `:cancelled`. Transitions beyond create/cancel belong
  to other contexts (time tracking clocks a job into `:in_progress`).

  ## Pay fields

  `pay_type`/`hourly_rate_cents`/`piece_rate_cents` describe what the
  *cleaner* earns for this job — as distinct from `agreed_price_cents`,
  what the *client* is charged. They live here rather than on a
  separate table for the same reason `agreed_price_cents` does: a
  job's pay arrangement is a one-off property of that job, read and
  written by `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking` rather than by Scheduling
  itself.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          status: :scheduled | :in_progress | :completed | :cancelled,
          agreed_price_cents: integer() | nil,
          pay_type: :hourly | :piece_rate | nil,
          hourly_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          piece_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "jobs" do
    field :scheduled_date, :date
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time

    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:scheduled, :in_progress, :completed, :cancelled],
      default: :scheduled

    field :agreed_price_cents, :integer
    field :agreed_price, :decimal, virtual: true

    field :pay_type, Ecto.Enum, values: [:hourly, :piece_rate]
    field :hourly_rate_cents, :integer
    field :piece_rate_cents, :integer

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :recurring_plan, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(client_id property_id cleaner_id recurring_plan_id scheduled_date
             start_time end_time status agreed_price_cents agreed_price
             pay_type hourly_rate_cents piece_rate_cents)a

  def changeset(job, attrs) do
    job
    |> cast(rename_date_key(attrs), @fields)
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])
    |> validate_time_order()
    |> put_agreed_price_cents()
  end

  # The board's own job form asks for a plain "date" — friendlier than
  # "scheduled date" — while some spex drive the same form with a
  # `scheduled_date` override instead (matching the schema field name
  # directly). The form carries a second, always-blank
  # `job[scheduled_date]` field purely as a landing pad for that
  # override key (`Phoenix.LiveViewTest.form/3` requires an override's
  # key to match a real field name in the form). Whichever one arrives
  # non-blank wins; `scheduled_date` takes precedence when both do,
  # since a still-blank landing pad means only `date` was ever touched.
  defp rename_date_key(%{"scheduled_date" => sd} = attrs) when sd not in [nil, ""],
    do: Map.delete(attrs, "date")

  defp rename_date_key(%{scheduled_date: sd} = attrs) when sd not in [nil, ""],
    do: Map.delete(attrs, :date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{"date" => date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete("date") |> Map.put("scheduled_date", date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{date: date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete(:date) |> Map.put(:scheduled_date, date)

  defp rename_date_key(attrs), do: attrs

  defp validate_time_order(changeset) do
    start_time = get_field(changeset, :start_time)
    end_time = get_field(changeset, :end_time)

    if start_time && end_time && Time.compare(start_time, end_time) != :lt do
      add_error(changeset, :end_time, "must be after the start time")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  # `agreed_price` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the
  # money-handling ADR's rate math); it is rounded half-up and stored
  # as `agreed_price_cents` — the only column ever persisted.
  defp put_agreed_price_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :agreed_price) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :agreed_price_cents, cents)
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quality do
  @moduledoc """
  Room-by-room checklists instantiated per job, before/after photo
  proof, incident reports (damage, missing items, unsafe conditions),
  and the scorecards that aggregate a cleaner's completed jobs.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  alias CleanerCrm.Quality.{
    Checklist,
    ChecklistItem,
    ChecklistTemplate,
    IncidentReport,
    Photo,
    Scorecard
  }

  ## Checklist templates

  def list_checklist_templates(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    ChecklistTemplate
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([t], asc: t.name)
    |> preload(:property)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_checklist_template!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    ChecklistTemplate
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload(:property)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_checklist_template(%Scope{}, %ChecklistTemplate{} = template, attrs \\ %{}) do
    ChecklistTemplate.changeset(template, attrs)
  end

  def create_checklist_template(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %ChecklistTemplate{account_id: account_id}
    |> ChecklistTemplate.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  def update_checklist_template(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        %ChecklistTemplate{} = template,
        attrs
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    template
    |> ChecklistTemplate.changeset(attrs)

  with job (and its client), cleaner, and photos preloaded.

    IncidentReport
    |> where([r], r.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([r], desc: r.filed_at)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :photos, job: [:client, :property]])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  The cleaner's average quality score and trend across their
  completed jobs, oldest first (see `CleanerCrm.Quality.Scorecard`).
  """
  def cleaner_scorecard(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Checklist
    |> join(:inner, [c], j in Job, on: j.id == c.job_id)

    |> order_by([c], asc: c.completed_at)
    |> select([c], c.quality_score)
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.reject(&is_nil/1)
    |> Scorecard.aggregate()
  end

  `:description`; a `:photo` (the same attrs `attach_photo/4` takes)
  is required unless `:type` is `"unsafe_condition"`. The cleaner and
  filing time are always the caller's and now — never accepted from
  `attrs` — and nothing about a filed report can change afterward.
  """
  def file_incident_report(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id, user: user}, %Job{} = job, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    {photo_attrs, report_attrs} = attrs |> stringify_keys() |> Map.pop("photo")

    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, report} <-
             %IncidentReport{account_id: account_id}
             |> IncidentReport.changeset(
               Map.merge(report_attrs, %{
                 "job_id" => job.id,
                 "cleaner_id" => user && user.id,
                 "filed_at" => DateTime.utc_now()
               }),
               not is_nil(photo_attrs)
             )
             |> Repo.insert() do
        photo = photo_attrs && insert_incident_photo!(account_id, report, photo_attrs)
        {:ok, %{report | photos: Enum.filter([photo], & &1)}}
      end
    end)
  end

  defp stringify_keys(attrs), do: Map.new(attrs, fn {key, value} -> {to_string(key), value} end)

  defp insert_incident_photo!(account_id, %IncidentReport{} = report, photo_attrs) do
    %Photo{account_id: account_id}
    |> Photo.changeset(
      Map.merge(stringify_keys(photo_attrs), %{
        "incident_report_id" => report.id,
        "kind" => "incident",
        "upload_state" => "uploaded",
        "captured_at" => DateTime.utc_now()
      })
    )
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists an account's incident reports, most recently filed first,
  with job (and its client), cleaner, and photos preloaded.
  """
  def list_incident_reports(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    IncidentReport
    |> where([r], r.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([r], desc: r.filed_at)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :photos, job: [:client, :property]])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Scorecards

  @doc """
  The cleaner's average quality score and trend across their
  completed jobs, oldest first (see `CleanerCrm.Quality.Scorecard`).
  """
  def cleaner_scorecard(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Checklist
    |> join(:inner, [c], j in Job, on: j.id == c.job_id)
    |> where(
      [c, j],
      c.account_id == ^account_id and j.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and
        not is_nil(c.completed_at)
    )
    |> order_by([c], asc: c.completed_at)
    |> select([c], c.quality_score)
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.reject(&is_nil/1)
    |> Scorecard.aggregate()
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.InvoiceLive.Show do @moduledoc """ Invoice detail: amount, payment status, proof-of-work from Quality for chargeback defense, and payment actions (charge the card on file, retry after a decline, or send a payment link). Per the payments-stripe ADR the invoice itself only ever changes status on a Stripe webhook confirmation — never synchronously from these buttons, so clicking "charge" here doesn't mark it paid. ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Billing` - `CleanerCrm.Quality` (proof-of-work only) """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view alias CleanerCrm.Billing alias CleanerCrm.Money alias CleanerCrm.Quality @impl true def render(assigns) do ~H""" <.header> Invoice for {client_name(@invoice)} <:subtitle> {Money.format_cents(@invoice.amount_cents)} · {status_label(@invoice.status)}
<.button :if={can_charge_card?(@invoice, @client)} data-test="charge-card-button" phx-click="charge_card" > Charge card on file <.button :if={can_retry_charge?(@invoice, @client)} data-test="retry-charge-button" phx-click="charge_card" > Retry charge <.button :if={@invoice.status == :unpaid} data-test="send-payment-link-button" phx-click="send_payment_link" > Send payment link

Share this payment link with the client:

{@payment_path}
<.header>Proof of Work

No completed checklist recorded.

  • {item.task}
""" end @impl true def mount(%{"id" => id}, _session, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope invoice = Billing.get_invoice!(scope, id) {:ok, socket |> assign(:invoice, invoice) |> assign(:client, invoice.job.client) |> assign(:page_title, "Invoice") |> assign(:payment_path, payment_path(invoice)) |> assign(:checklist_items, checklist_items(scope, invoice.job))} end @impl true def handle_event("charge_card", _params, socket) do case Billing.charge_card(socket.assigns.current_scope, socket.assigns.invoice) do {:ok, invoice} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :invoice, invoice)} {:error, reason} -> {:noreply, put_flash(socket, :error, charge_error_message(reason))} end end def handle_event("send_payment_link", _params, socket) do {:ok, invoice} = Billing.create_payment_link(socket.assigns.current_scope, socket.assigns.invoice) {:noreply, socket |> assign(:invoice, invoice) |> assign(:payment_path, payment_path(invoice))} end defp payment_path(%{payment_token: nil}), do: nil defp payment_path(%{payment_token: token}), do: ~p"/pay/#{token}" defp client_name(%{job: %{client: %{name: name}}}), do: name defp client_name(_invoice), do: "—" defp can_charge_card?(invoice, client) do invoice.status == :unpaid and card_on_file?(client) and is_nil(invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id) end defp can_retry_charge?(invoice, client) do invoice.status == :unpaid and card_on_file?(client) and not is_nil(invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id) end defp card_on_file?(nil), do: false defp card_on_file?(client), do: client.card_on_file defp charge_error_message(:no_card_on_file), do: "This client has no card on file." defp charge_error_message(%{"code" => "card_declined"}) do "The card was declined. Try again or send a payment link instead." end defp charge_error_message(_reason) do "Unable to charge the card on file right now. Please try again shortly." end defp status_label(:unpaid), do: "Unpaid" defp status_label(:charge_pending), do: "Charge Pending" defp status_label(:paid), do: "Paid" defp checklist_items(scope, job) do case Quality.get_checklist_for_job(scope, job) do %{items: items} -> items nil -> [] end end end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quality.Photo do
  @moduledoc """
  A stored before/after (checklist proof) or incident photo, with
  offline-tolerant upload state.

  Per the file-storage ADR, uploads land in S3-compatible object
  storage via presigned URLs from the phone — a `Photo` row exists
  from the moment the cleaner picks the file (`:pending`, no
  `storage_key` yet) so a dropped connection just leaves it pending
  until the retry lands (`:uploaded`, `storage_key` set).
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type kind :: :before | :after | :incident
  @type upload_state :: :pending | :uploaded

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          checklist_item_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          incident_report_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          kind: kind() | nil,
          upload_state: upload_state(),
          storage_key: String.t() | nil,
          captured_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "photos" do
    field :kind, Ecto.Enum, values: [:before, :after, :incident]
    field :upload_state, Ecto.Enum, values: [:pending, :uploaded], default: :pending
    field :storage_key, :string
    field :captured_at, :utc_datetime_usec

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :checklist_item, CleanerCrm.Quality.ChecklistItem, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :incident_report, CleanerCrm.Quality.IncidentReport, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  def changeset(photo, attrs) do
    photo
    |> cast(attrs, [
      :account_id,
      :checklist_item_id,
      :incident_report_id,
      :kind,
      :upload_state,
      :storage_key,
      :captured_at
    ])
    |> validate_required([:account_id, :kind])
    |> validate_one_owner()
  end

  @doc "Flips a pending photo to uploaded once its bytes land in storage."
  def uploaded_changeset(photo, storage_key) do
    change(photo, upload_state: :uploaded, storage_key: storage_key)
  end

  defp validate_one_owner(changeset) do
    case {get_field(changeset, :checklist_item_id), get_field(changeset, :incident_report_id)} do
      {nil, nil} ->
        add_error(changeset, :checklist_item_id, "or incident_report_id is required")

      {_id, nil} ->
        changeset

      {nil, _id} ->
        changeset

      {_checklist_item_id, _incident_report_id} ->
        add_error(changeset, :checklist_item_id, "and incident_report_id cannot both be set")
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quality.ChecklistItem do
  @moduledoc """
  A single room/task line on a job's checklist: its required flag,
  checked/skipped completion state, and the before/after photos
  attached to it as proof.

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  alias CleanerCrm.Quality.Photo

          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          checklist_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          room: String.t() | nil,
          task: String.t() | nil,
          required: boolean(),
          checked: boolean(),
          checked_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          skipped: boolean(),
          skip_reason: String.t() | nil,
          position: integer(),
          photos: [Photo.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "checklist_items" do
    field :room, :string
    field :task, :string
    field :required, :boolean, default: true
    field :checked, :boolean, default: false
    field :checked_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :skipped, :boolean, default: false
    field :skip_reason, :string
    field :position, :integer, default: 0

    belongs_to :checklist, CleanerCrm.Quality.Checklist, type: :binary_id
    has_many :photos, Photo

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  def changeset(item, attrs) do
    item
    |> cast(attrs, [:checklist_id, :room, :task, :required, :position])
    |> validate_required([:checklist_id, :task])
  end

  @doc "Checks the item off, stamping when, and clears any prior skip."
  def check_changeset(item) do
    change(item, checked: true, checked_at: DateTime.utc_now(), skipped: false, skip_reason: nil)
  end

  @doc "Reverts a checked item back to unchecked."
  def uncheck_changeset(item) do
    change(item, checked: false, checked_at: nil)
  end

  @doc "Marks a required item skipped, with a reason, instead of done."
  def skip_changeset(item, reason) do
    item
    |> change(skipped: true, skip_reason: reason, checked: false, checked_at: nil)
    |> validate_required([:skip_reason])
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quality.Checklist do
  @moduledoc """
  The instantiated checklist for a single job: its items, the
  owner's optional 1-5 rating, and the computed quality score (see
  `CleanerCrm.Quality.Scorecard`). Functions that need `items` for
  scoring or completion gating expect them preloaded, as returned by
  `CleanerCrm.Quality.get_checklist_for_job/2`.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  alias CleanerCrm.Quality.ChecklistItem

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          job_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          checklist_template_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          owner_rating: integer() | nil,
          quality_score: float() | nil,
          completed_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          items: [ChecklistItem.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "checklists" do
    field :owner_rating, :integer
    field :quality_score, :float
    field :completed_at, :utc_datetime_usec

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :job, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :checklist_template, CleanerCrm.Quality.ChecklistTemplate, type: :binary_id

    has_many :items, ChecklistItem, preload_order: [asc: :position]

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  def changeset(checklist, attrs) do
    checklist
    |> cast(attrs, [
      :job_id,
      :checklist_template_id,
      :owner_rating,
      :quality_score,
      :completed_at
    ])
    |> validate_required([:job_id])
    |> validate_number(:owner_rating, greater_than_or_equal_to: 1, less_than_or_equal_to: 5)
    |> unique_constraint(:job_id)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Clients do
  @moduledoc """
  Clients and their properties: addresses, parking notes, entry
  methods and codes, pets, and cleaning preferences — the authoritative
  access and scope record every job carries.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.{Client, Property}
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder

  ## Clients

  def list_clients(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do

defmodule CleanerCrm.Money do
  @moduledoc """
  Formats integer cents for display, per the money-handling ADR: every
  amount is stored and computed as integer cents, and this is the only
  place a dollar string gets built.
  """

  @doc """
  Formats integer cents as `"$X.XX"`, with thousands separators. `nil`
  is treated as zero.

  ## Examples

      iex> CleanerCrm.Money.format_cents(18_000)
      "$180.00"

      iex> CleanerCrm.Money.format_cents(nil)
      "$0.00"
  """
  @spec format_cents(integer() | nil) :: String.t()
  def format_cents(nil), do: format_cents(0)

  def format_cents(cents) when is_integer(cents) do
    sign = if cents < 0, do: "-", else: ""
    dollars = div(abs(cents), 100)
    remainder = rem(abs(cents), 100)

    "#{sign}$#{group_thousands(dollars)}.#{pad_cents(remainder)}"
  end

  defp pad_cents(remainder), do: remainder |> Integer.to_string() |> String.pad_leading(2, "0")

  defp group_thousands(dollars) do
    dollars
    |> Integer.to_string()
    |> String.reverse()
    |> String.replace(~r/(\d{3})(?=\d)/, "\\1,")
    |> String.reverse()
  end
end

  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, _token, _params, _), do: conn

  defp write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token) do
    conn
    |> put_session(:user_remember_me, true)
    |> put_resp_cookie(@remember_me_cookie, token, @remember_me_options)
  end

  defp put_token_in_session(conn, token) do
    conn
    |> put_session(:user_token, token)
    |> put_session(:live_socket_id, user_session_topic(token))
  end

  @doc """
  Disconnects existing sockets for the given tokens.
  """
  def disconnect_sessions(tokens) do
    Enum.each(tokens, fn %{token: token} ->
      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.broadcast(user_session_topic(token), "disconnect", %{})
    end)
  end

  defp user_session_topic(token), do: "users_sessions:#{Base.url_encode64(token)}"

  @doc """
  Handles mounting and authenticating the current_scope in LiveViews.

  ## `on_mount` arguments

    * `:mount_current_scope` - Assigns current_scope
      to socket assigns based on user_token, or nil if
      there's no user_token or no matching user.

    * `:require_authenticated` - Authenticates the user from the session,
      and assigns the current_scope to socket assigns based
      on user_token.
      Redirects to login page if there's no logged user.

  ## Examples

  Use the `on_mount` lifecycle macro in LiveViews to mount or authenticate
  the `current_scope`:

      defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PageLive do
        use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view

        on_mount {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}
        ...
      end

  Or use the `live_session` of your router to invoke the on_mount callback:

      live_session :authenticated, on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
        live "/profile", ProfileLive, :index
      end
  """
  def on_mount(:mount_current_scope, _params, session, socket) do
    {:cont, mount_current_scope(socket, session)}
  end

  def on_mount(:require_authenticated, _params, session, socket) do
    socket = mount_current_scope(socket, session)

    if socket.assigns.current_scope && socket.assigns.current_scope.user do
      {:cont, socket}
    else
      socket =
        socket
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "You must log in to access this page.")
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")

      {:halt, socket}
    end
  end

  def on_mount(:require_sudo_mode, _params, session, socket) do
    socket = mount_current_scope(socket, session)

    if Users.sudo_mode?(socket.assigns.current_scope.user, -10) do
      {:cont, socket}
    else
      socket =
        socket
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "You must re-authenticate to access this page.")
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")

      {:halt, socket}
    end
  end

  defp mount_current_scope(socket, session) do
    Phoenix.Component.assign_new(socket, :current_scope, fn ->
      {user, _} =
        if user_token = session["user_token"] do
          Users.get_user_by_session_token(user_token)
        end || {nil, nil}

      scope_with_active_account(user)
    end)
  end

  # There's no persisted "current account" selection yet (the account
  # picker doesn't write one anywhere), so every account-scoped page

defmodule CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase do
  @moduledoc """
  This module defines the test case to be used by
  tests that require setting up a connection.

  Such tests rely on `Phoenix.ConnTest` and also
  import other functionality to make it easier
  to build common data structures and query the data layer.

  Finally, if the test case interacts with the database,
  we enable the SQL sandbox, so changes done to the database
  are reverted at the end of every test. If you are using
  PostgreSQL, you can even run database tests asynchronously
  by setting `use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true`, although
  this option is not recommended for other databases.
  """

  use ExUnit.CaseTemplate

  using do
    quote do
      # The default endpoint for testing
      @endpoint CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint

      use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

      # Import conveniences for testing with connections
      import Plug.Conn
      import Phoenix.ConnTest
      import CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase
    end
  end

  setup tags do
    CleanerCrmTest.DataCase.setup_sandbox(tags)
    {:ok, conn: Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()}
  end

  @doc """
  Setup helper that registers and logs in users.

      setup :register_and_log_in_user

  It stores an updated connection and a registered user in the
  test context.
  """
  def register_and_log_in_user(%{conn: conn} = context) do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture()
    scope = CleanerCrm.Users.Scope.for_user(user)

    opts =
      context
      |> Map.take([:token_authenticated_at])
      |> Enum.into([])

    %{conn: log_in_user(conn, user, opts), user: user, scope: scope}
  end

  @doc """
  Logs the given `user` into the `conn`.

  It returns an updated `conn`.
  """
  def log_in_user(conn, user, opts \\ []) do
    token = CleanerCrm.Users.generate_user_session_token(user)

    maybe_set_token_authenticated_at(token, opts[:token_authenticated_at])

    conn
    |> Phoenix.ConnTest.init_test_session(%{})
    |> Plug.Conn.put_session(:user_token, token)
  end

  defp maybe_set_token_authenticated_at(_token, nil), do: nil

  defp maybe_set_token_authenticated_at(token, authenticated_at) do
    CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.override_token_authenticated_at(token, authenticated_at)
  end
end
