defmodule CleanerCrm.Users.UserToken do
  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Query
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.UserToken

  @hash_algorithm :sha256
  @rand_size 32

  # It is very important to keep the magic link token expiry short,
  # since someone with access to the email may take over the account.
  @magic_link_validity_in_minutes 15
  @change_email_validity_in_days 7
  @session_validity_in_days 14

  schema "users_tokens" do
    field :token, :binary
    field :context, :string
    field :sent_to, :string
    field :authenticated_at, :utc_datetime
    belongs_to :user, CleanerCrm.Users.User

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime, updated_at: false)
  end

  @doc """
  Generates a token that will be stored in a signed place,
  such as session or cookie. As they are signed, those
  tokens do not need to be hashed.

  The reason why we store session tokens in the database, even
  though Phoenix already provides a session cookie, is because
  Phoenix's default session cookies are not persisted, they are
  simply signed and potentially encrypted. This means they are
  valid indefinitely, unless you change the signing/encryption
  salt.

  Therefore, storing them allows individual user
  sessions to be expired. The token system can also be extended
  to store additional data, such as the device used for logging in.
  You could then use this information to display all valid sessions
  and devices in the UI and allow users to explicitly expire any
  session they deem invalid.
  """
  def build_session_token(user) do
    token = :crypto.strong_rand_bytes(@rand_size)
    dt = user.authenticated_at || DateTime.utc_now(:second)
    {token, %UserToken{token: token, context: "session", user_id: user.id, authenticated_at: dt}}
  end

  @doc """
  Checks if the token is valid and returns its underlying lookup query.

  The query returns the user found by the token, if any, along with the token's creation time.

  The token is valid if it matches the value in the database and it has
  not expired (after @session_validity_in_days).
  """
  def verify_session_token_query(token) do
    query =
      from token in by_token_and_context_query(token, "session"),
        join: user in assoc(token, :user),
        where: token.inserted_at > ago(@session_validity_in_days, "day"),
        select: {%{user | authenticated_at: token.authenticated_at}, token.inserted_at}

    {:ok, query}
  end

  @doc """
  Builds a token and its hash to be delivered to the user's email.

  The non-hashed token is sent to the user email while the
  hashed part is stored in the database. The original token cannot be reconstructed,
  which means anyone with read-only access to the database cannot directly use
  the token in the application to gain access. Furthermore, if the user changes
  their email in the system, the tokens sent to the previous email are no longer
  valid.

  Users can easily adapt the existing code to provide other types of delivery methods,
  for example, by phone numbers.
  """
  def build_email_token(user, context) do
    build_hashed_token(user, context, user.email)
  end

  defp build_hashed_token(user, context, sent_to) do
    token = :crypto.strong_rand_bytes(@rand_size)
    hashed_token = :crypto.hash(@hash_algorithm, token)

    {Base.url_encode64(token, padding: false),
     %UserToken{
       token: hashed_token,
       context: context,
       sent_to: sent_to,
       user_id: user.id
     }}
  end

  @doc """
  Checks if the token is valid and returns its underlying lookup query.

  If found, the query returns a tuple of the form `{user, token}`.

  The given token is valid if it matches its hashed counterpart in the
  database. This function also checks whether the token has expired. The context
  of a magic link token is always "login".
  """
  def verify_magic_link_token_query(token) do
    case Base.url_decode64(token, padding: false) do
      {:ok, decoded_token} ->
        hashed_token = :crypto.hash(@hash_algorithm, decoded_token)

        query =
          from token in by_token_and_context_query(hashed_token, "login"),
            join: user in assoc(token, :user),
            where: token.inserted_at > ago(^@magic_link_validity_in_minutes, "minute"),
            where: token.sent_to == user.email,
            select: {user, token}

        {:ok, query}

      :error ->
        :error
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Checks if the token is valid and returns its underlying lookup query.

  The query returns the user_token found by the token, if any.

  This is used to validate requests to change the user
  email.
  The given token is valid if it matches its hashed counterpart in the
  database and if it has not expired (after @change_email_validity_in_days).
  The context must always start with "change:".
  """
  def verify_change_email_token_query(token, "change:" <> _ = context) do
    case Base.url_decode64(token, padding: false) do
      {:ok, decoded_token} ->
        hashed_token = :crypto.hash(@hash_algorithm, decoded_token)

        query =
          from token in by_token_and_context_query(hashed_token, context),
            where: token.inserted_at > ago(@change_email_validity_in_days, "day")

        {:ok, query}

      :error ->
        :error
    end
  end

  defp by_token_and_context_query(token, context) do
    from UserToken, where: [token: ^token, context: ^context]
  end
end

  Generates a token that will be stored in a signed place,
  such as session or cookie. As they are signed, those
  tokens do not need to be hashed.

  The reason why we store session tokens in the database, even
  though Phoenix already provides a session cookie, is because
  Phoenix's default session cookies are not persisted, they are
  simply signed and potentially encrypted. This means they are
  valid indefinitely, unless you change the signing/encryption
  salt.

  Therefore, storing them allows individual user
  sessions to be expired. The token system can also be extended
  to store additional data, such as the device used for logging in.
  You could then use this information to display all valid sessions
  and devices in the UI and allow users to explicitly expire any
  session they deem invalid.
  """
  def build_session_token(user) do
    token = :crypto.strong_rand_bytes(@rand_size)
    dt = user.authenticated_at || DateTime.utc_now(:second)
    {token, %UserToken{token: token, context: "session", user_id: user.id, authenticated_at: dt}}
  end

  @doc """
  Checks if the token is valid and returns its underlying lookup query.

  The query returns the user found by the token, if any, along with the token's creation time.

  The token is valid if it matches the value in the database and it has
  not expired (after @session_validity_in_days).
  """
  def verify_session_token_query(token) do
    query =
      from token in by_token_and_context_query(token, "session"),
        join: user in assoc(token, :user),
        where: token.inserted_at > ago(@session_validity_in_days, "day"),
        select: {%{user | authenticated_at: token.authenticated_at}, token.inserted_at}

    {:ok, query}
  end

  @doc """
  Builds a token and its hash to be delivered to the user's email.

  The non-hashed token is sent to the user email while the
  hashed part is stored in the database. The original token cannot be reconstructed,
  which means anyone with read-only access to the database cannot directly use
  the token in the application to gain access. Furthermore, if the user changes
  their email in the system, the tokens sent to the previous email are no longer
  valid.

  Users can easily adapt the existing code to provide other types of delivery methods,
  for example, by phone numbers.
  """
  def build_email_token(user, context) do
    build_hashed_token(user, context, user.email)
  end

  defp build_hashed_token(user, context, sent_to) do
    token = :crypto.strong_rand_bytes(@rand_size)
    hashed_token = :crypto.hash(@hash_algorithm, token)

    {Base.url_encode64(token, padding: false),
     %UserToken{
       token: hashed_token,
       context: context,
       sent_to: sent_to,
       user_id: user.id
     }}
  end

  @doc """
  Checks if the token is valid and returns its underlying lookup query.

  If found, the query returns a tuple of the form `{user, token}`.

  The given token is valid if it matches its hashed counterpart in the
  database. This function also checks whether the token has expired. The context
  of a magic link token is always "login".
  """
  def verify_magic_link_token_query(token) do
    case Base.url_decode64(token, padding: false) do
      {:ok, decoded_token} ->
        hashed_token = :crypto.hash(@hash_algorithm, decoded_token)

        query =
          from token in by_token_and_context_query(hashed_token, "login"),
            join: user in assoc(token, :user),
            where: token.inserted_at > ago(^@magic_link_validity_in_minutes, "minute"),
            where: token.sent_to == user.email,
            select: {user, token}

        {:ok, query}

      :error ->
        :error
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Checks if the token is valid and returns its underlying lookup query.

  The query returns the user_token found by the token, if any.

  This is used to validate requests to change the user
  email.
  The given token is valid if it matches its hashed counterpart in the
  database and if it has not expired (after @change_email_validity_in_days).
  The context must always start with "change:".
  """
  def verify_change_email_token_query(token, "change:" <> _ = context) do
    case Base.url_decode64(token, padding: false) do
      {:ok, decoded_token} ->
        hashed_token = :crypto.hash(@hash_algorithm, decoded_token)

        query =
          from token in by_token_and_context_query(hashed_token, context),
            where: token.inserted_at > ago(@change_email_validity_in_days, "day")

        {:ok, query}

      :error ->
        :error
    end
  end

  defp by_token_and_context_query(token, context) do
    from UserToken, where: [token: ^token, context: ^context]
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Users.User do
  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  schema "users" do
    field :email, :string
    field :name, :string
    field :password, :string, virtual: true, redact: true
    field :hashed_password, :string, redact: true
    field :confirmed_at, :utc_datetime
    field :authenticated_at, :utc_datetime, virtual: true
    field :push_enabled, :boolean, default: true

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime)
  end

  @doc """
  A user changeset for registering or changing the email.

  It requires the email to change otherwise an error is added.

  Also casts `:push_enabled` — there's no dedicated settings changeset
  for it, and this is the only changeset `register_user/1` runs, so
  it's the one path that lets a cleaner fixture seed the preference.

  ## Options

    * `:validate_unique` - Set to false if you don't want to validate the
      uniqueness of the email, useful when displaying live validations.
      Defaults to `true`.
  """
  def email_changeset(user, attrs, opts \\ []) do
    user
    |> cast(attrs, [:email, :push_enabled])
    |> validate_email(opts)
  end

  defp validate_email(changeset, opts) do
    changeset =
      changeset
      |> validate_required([:email])
      |> validate_format(:email, ~r/^[^@,;\s]+@[^@,;\s]+$/,
        message: "must have the @ sign and no spaces"
      )
      |> validate_length(:email, max: 160)

    if Keyword.get(opts, :validate_unique, true) do
      changeset
      |> unsafe_validate_unique(:email, CleanerCrm.Repo)
      |> unique_constraint(:email)
      |> validate_email_changed()
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  defp validate_email_changed(changeset) do
    if get_field(changeset, :email) && get_change(changeset, :email) == nil do
      add_error(changeset, :email, "did not change")
    else

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing.ReceiptNotifier do
  @moduledoc """
  Emails the client a receipt once a card-on-file or payment-link
  charge has been submitted to Stripe — submitted, not confirmed; per
  the payments-stripe ADR the invoice itself only becomes `:paid` on
  the webhook.
  """

  import Swoosh.Email

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.Invoice
  alias CleanerCrm.Mailer
  alias CleanerCrm.Money

  def deliver_receipt(email, %Invoice{} = invoice) when is_binary(email) do
    message =
      new()
      |> to(email)
      |> from({"CleanerCrm", "contact@example.com"})
      |> subject("Your receipt")
      |> text_body("""
      Thanks! We've charged #{Money.format_cents(invoice.amount_cents)} for your recent cleaning.

      This confirms the charge was submitted — you'll receive nothing further unless it's declined.
      """)

    Mailer.deliver(message)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing.Payment do
  @moduledoc """
  A single payment attempt against an invoice — the audit trail behind
  an invoice's current status. Kept separate from `Invoice` so a
  declined attempt and a later successful retry both stay on the
  record, instead of one row's history being overwritten.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type status :: :pending | :succeeded | :failed
  @type source :: String.t()

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          invoice_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          amount_cents: integer() | nil,
          status: status(),
          provider: String.t(),
          stripe_payment_intent_id: String.t() | nil,
          source: source() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "payments" do
    field :amount_cents, :integer
    field :status, Ecto.Enum, values: [:pending, :succeeded, :failed], default: :pending
    field :provider, :string, default: "stripe"
    field :stripe_payment_intent_id, :string
    field :source, :string

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :invoice, CleanerCrm.Billing.Invoice, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(invoice_id amount_cents status provider stripe_payment_intent_id source)a

  def changeset(payment, attrs) do
    payment
    |> cast(attrs, @fields)
    |> validate_required([:invoice_id, :amount_cents, :status])
  end
end

# LiveView Design Documentation Rules

## Purpose
These rules ensure consistent, complete design documentation for Phoenix LiveViews and components before implementation.

## Design System

Before building any UI, read `.code_my_spec/design/design_system.html` for the project's design system. Use the DaisyUI component classes and theme tokens defined there. Do not invent custom colors or component patterns that deviate from the design system.

## Guidelines

Keep liveviews small and focused.
Each liveview should correspond to a path. No modifying the UI implicitly without a path change.

## LiveView Design Template

### File Structure
- Place in `docs/design/my_app_web/{context}_live/`
- Name files by function: `index.md`, `show.md`, `form.md`

### Required Sections

1. **Purpose** - Single sentence/short paragraph describing what this LiveView does
2. **Route** - The URL pattern that renders this LiveView
3. **Context Access** - List the context functions this LiveView calls
4. **LiveView Structure** - Three subsections:
   - **Mount** - What happens when LiveView initializes
   - **Events** - User interactions and their handlers
   - **Template** - UI structure and components used
5. **Data Flow** - Numbered steps of the user journey
6. **Security** - Permission checks and authorization rules
7. **Real-time Updates** - PubSub subscriptions and live updates (if applicable)

## Style Guidelines

- **Be concise** - Each section should be brief but complete
- **Use bullets** - Structure information as bullet points
- **Include context calls** - Show exactly which context functions are used
- **Show code examples** - Provide HEEx usage examples for components
- **Focus on behavior** - Describe what happens, not how it's implemented
- **Consider security** - Always include permission and authorization concerns
- **Plan for real-time** - Consider PubSub integration for live updates

5	## Phoenix 1.8 Form Component Pattern
6	
7	**Structure**: Create a single LiveView module handling both `:new` and `:edit` actions with these required elements:
8	
9	1. **Module Setup**
10	   ```elixir
11	   defmodule AppWeb.ResourceLive.Form do
12	     use AppWeb, :live_view
13	     alias App.Context
14	     alias App.Context.Schema
15	   ```
16	
17	2. **Required Functions**
18	   - `render/1` - Form template with `phx-change="validate"` and `phx-submit="save"`
19	   - `mount/3` - Extract `return_to` param and call `apply_action/3`
20	   - `apply_action/3` - Pattern match on `:new`/`:edit`, set page title, schema, and form
21	   - `handle_event/3` - Handle "validate" and "save" events
22	   - `save_resource/3` - Pattern match on action, call context create/update functions
23	
24	3. **Key Patterns**
25	   - Use `to_form(changeset)` for form assignment
26	   - Handle validation with `action: :validate` on changeset errors
27	   - Navigate on success with `push_navigate/2`
28	   - Support `return_to` parameter for flexible navigation
29	   - Use consistent flash messages: "Resource created/updated successfully"

session_type: "code"
---
## Phoenix 1.8 Form Component Pattern

**Structure**: Create a single LiveView module handling both `:new` and `:edit` actions with these required elements:

1. **Module Setup**
   ```elixir
   defmodule AppWeb.ResourceLive.Form do
     use AppWeb, :live_view
     alias App.Context
     alias App.Context.Schema
   ```

2. **Required Functions**
   - `render/1` - Form template with `phx-change="validate"` and `phx-submit="save"`
   - `mount/3` - Extract `return_to` param and call `apply_action/3`
   - `apply_action/3` - Pattern match on `:new`/`:edit`, set page title, schema, and form
   - `handle_event/3` - Handle "validate" and "save" events
   - `save_resource/3` - Pattern match on action, call context create/update functions

3. **Key Patterns**
   - Use `to_form(changeset)` for form assignment
   - Handle validation with `action: :validate` on changeset errors
   - Navigate on success with `push_navigate/2`
   - Support `return_to` parameter for flexible navigation
   - Use consistent flash messages: "Resource created/updated successfully"

4. **Template Requirements**
   - Wrap in layout component with flash and current_scope
   - Include header with dynamic page title
   - Form with proper field inputs and submit/cancel buttons
   - Cancel button navigates to computed return path

This pattern ensures consistent CRUD form behavior across your Phoenix 1.8 application.

# Phoenix Live Context Design Rules

## Naming Convention
- Use `AppWeb.{Feature}Live` as the namespace (e.g., `MyAppWeb.UserLive`)
- Child LiveViews use action suffixes: `UserLive.Index`, `UserLive.Show`, `UserLive.Edit`
- Child LiveComponents use descriptive names: `UserLive.FormComponent`, `UserLive.FilterComponent`

## Structure
- Each child LiveView corresponds to a unique route
- LiveComponents are shared across views in this context
- The live context itself has no code file — it is a spec-only grouping

## Scope
- Focus on a single feature area (users, accounts, orders)
- Keep the number of children manageable (typically 2-5 views + 0-3 shared components)
- Dependencies should point to domain contexts, not other live contexts

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb do
  @moduledoc """
  The entrypoint for defining your web interface, such
  as controllers, components, channels, and so on.

  This can be used in your application as:

      use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller
      use CleanerCrmWeb, :html

  The definitions below will be executed for every controller,
  component, etc, so keep them short and clean, focused
  on imports, uses and aliases.

  Do NOT define functions inside the quoted expressions
  below. Instead, define additional modules and import
  those modules here.
  """

  use Boundary, deps: [CleanerCrm], exports: :all

  def static_paths, do: ~w(assets fonts images favicon.ico robots.txt)

  def router do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Router, helpers: false

      # Import common connection and controller functions to use in pipelines
      import Plug.Conn
      import Phoenix.Controller
      import Phoenix.LiveView.Router
    end
  end

  def channel do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Channel
    end
  end

  def controller do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Controller, formats: [:html, :json]

      use Gettext, backend: CleanerCrmWeb.Gettext

      import Plug.Conn

      unquote(verified_routes())
    end
  end

  def live_view do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.LiveView

      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  def live_component do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.LiveComponent

      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  def html do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Component

      # Import convenience functions from controllers
      import Phoenix.Controller,
        only: [get_csrf_token: 0, view_module: 1, view_template: 1]

      # Include general helpers for rendering HTML
      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  defp html_helpers do
    quote do
      # Translation
      use Gettext, backend: CleanerCrmWeb.Gettext

      # HTML escaping functionality
      import Phoenix.HTML
      # Core UI components
      import CleanerCrmWeb.CoreComponents

      # Common modules used in templates
      alias Phoenix.LiveView.JS
      alias CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts

      # Routes generation with the ~p sigil
      unquote(verified_routes())
    end
  end

  def verified_routes do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.VerifiedRoutes,
        endpoint: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
        router: CleanerCrmWeb.Router,
        statics: CleanerCrmWeb.static_paths()
    end
  end

  @doc """
  When used, dispatch to the appropriate controller/live_view/etc.
  """
  defmacro __using__(which) when is_atom(which) do
    apply(__MODULE__, which, [])
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Portal.PortalSession do
  @moduledoc """
  A magic-link access token that lets a client into their portal with
  no password account.

  The plaintext token is only ever held in memory — in the `:token`
  virtual field, right after `build_changeset/2` creates it — to be
  mailed or handed to the client; only its SHA-256 hash is persisted.
  This mirrors `CleanerCrm.Users.UserToken`'s own magic-link scheme, so
  read access to the database alone can never reconstruct a working
  token.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @hash_algorithm :sha256
  @rand_size 32
  @default_validity_in_days 7

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          token: String.t() | nil,
          token_hash: binary() | nil,
          expires_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          last_used_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "portal_sessions" do
    field :token, :string, virtual: true
    field :token_hash, :binary
    field :expires_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :last_used_at, :utc_datetime_usec

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @doc """
  Builds a fresh session for `client`: a random plaintext token (held
  only in the returned changeset's `:token` virtual field, for the
  caller to mail or hand back) and its hash, expiring
  #{@default_validity_in_days} days out unless `attrs` gives its own
  `:expires_at`.
  """
  def build_changeset(%{id: client_id, account_id: account_id}, attrs) do
    token = generate_token()

    %__MODULE__{account_id: account_id, client_id: client_id}
    |> cast(attrs, [:expires_at, :last_used_at])
    |> put_change(:token, token)
    |> put_change(:token_hash, hash_token(token))
    |> put_default_expiry()
    |> validate_required([:account_id, :client_id, :token_hash, :expires_at])
  end

  @doc "Marks the session used just now."
  def touch_changeset(%__MODULE__{} = session) do
    change(session, last_used_at: DateTime.utc_now())
  end

  @doc "Hashes a plaintext token the same way `build_changeset/2` does, for lookup by token."
  def hash_token(token) when is_binary(token), do: :crypto.hash(@hash_algorithm, token)

  @doc "True once `expires_at` has passed."
  def expired?(%__MODULE__{expires_at: expires_at}),
    do: DateTime.compare(expires_at, DateTime.utc_now()) == :lt

  defp put_default_expiry(changeset) do
    case get_field(changeset, :expires_at) do
      nil ->
        put_change(
          changeset,
          :expires_at,
          DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), @default_validity_in_days, :day)
        )

      _expires_at ->
        changeset
    end
  end

  defp generate_token,
    do: @rand_size |> :crypto.strong_rand_bytes() |> Base.url_encode64(padding: false)
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Portal.CancellationPolicy do
  @moduledoc """
  Per-account reschedule/cancel policy: how much notice a client must
  give before a visit to cancel free of charge, the flat fee charged
  inside that window, the (typically higher) flat fee for a same-day
  cancellation, and the policy text shown to a client at booking.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          notice_window_hours: integer(),
          late_fee_cents: integer(),
          same_day_fee_cents: integer(),
          policy_text: String.t() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "cancellation_policies" do
    field :notice_window_hours, :integer, default: 24
    field :late_fee_cents, :integer, default: 0
    field :same_day_fee_cents, :integer, default: 0
    field :policy_text, :string

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(notice_window_hours late_fee_cents same_day_fee_cents policy_text)a

  def changeset(%__MODULE__{} = policy, attrs) do
    policy
    |> cast(attrs, @fields)
    |> validate_required([:notice_window_hours, :late_fee_cents, :same_day_fee_cents])

    |> validate_number(:late_fee_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> validate_number(:same_day_fee_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> unique_constraint(:account_id)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Portal do
  @moduledoc """
  Client-facing portal domain: magic-link session tokens for clients
  (no password accounts), the client's view of upcoming visits with
  assigned-cleaner identity, service history with proof-of-work, and
  self-service reschedule/cancel enforcement against the account's
  cancellation policy.

  Every function here takes a `CleanerCrm.Clients.Client` directly
  rather than a `CleanerCrm.Users.Scope` — a portal visitor is a
  client reached through a magic link, never a logged-in staff user.
  Internally, calls into `Scheduling`, `Quality`, `Billing`, and
  `Notifications` are scoped by deriving a `Scope` from the client's
  own `account_id`.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing
  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.Invoice
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications
  alias CleanerCrm.Portal.{CancellationPolicy, PortalSession, Tip}
  alias CleanerCrm.Quality
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  ## Magic-link sessions

  @doc """
  Issues a fresh portal session for `client`, returning the record
  with its plaintext `:token` set — the only time that token is ever
  available, so the caller (booking confirmation, "email me a link")
  must send or redirect with it immediately.
  """
  def create_portal_session(%Client{} = client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    client
    |> PortalSession.build_changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Exchanges a magic-link token for the client id it grants access to.
  Touches the session's `last_used_at` on success. Fails closed with
  `{:error, :invalid}` for a token that doesn't match any session, or
  one that's expired — a client offered the same "your link is
  invalid or expired" outcome either way, never told which.
  """
  def access_portal(token) when is_binary(token) do
    case Repo.get_by(PortalSession, token_hash: PortalSession.hash_token(token)) do
      nil -> {:error, :invalid}
      %PortalSession{} = session -> exchange(session)
    end
  end

  defp exchange(%PortalSession{} = session) do
    if PortalSession.expired?(session) do
      {:error, :invalid}
    else
      {:ok, _touched} = session |> PortalSession.touch_changeset() |> Repo.update()
      {:ok, session.client_id}
    end
  end

  @doc "Loads a client by id — the portal session carries only the id, never the whole struct."
  def get_client!(client_id), do: Repo.get!(Client, client_id)

  ## Visits

  @doc """
  The client's upcoming (today or later, not cancelled) visits,
  soonest first, cleaner preloaded for name/photo display.
  """
  def list_upcoming_visits(%Client{} = client) do
    client
    |> account_scope()
    |> Scheduling.list_jobs()
    |> Enum.filter(&(&1.client_id == client.id and &1.status in [:scheduled, :in_progress]))
    |> Enum.filter(&(Date.compare(&1.scheduled_date, Date.utc_today()) != :lt))
    |> Enum.sort_by(&{&1.scheduled_date, &1.start_time})
  end

  @doc """
  The client's completed visits, most recent first — each one's
  checklist and before/after photos are read separately via
  `visit_checklist/1`.
  """
  def list_visit_history(%Client{} = client) do
    client
    |> account_scope()
    |> Scheduling.list_jobs()
    |> Enum.filter(&(&1.client_id == client.id and &1.status == :completed))
    |> Enum.sort_by(& &1.scheduled_date, {:desc, Date})
  end

  @doc "A completed visit's checklist with items and photos preloaded, or `nil` if it has none."
  def visit_checklist(%Job{} = job) do
    Quality.get_checklist_for_job(system_scope(job.account_id), job)
  end

  @doc """
  Fetches a single visit for the portal's visit-detail page. Raises
  if `job_id` doesn't belong to `client` — the account-scoped lookup
  alone isn't enough, since other clients on the same account must
  never reach each other's visits by guessing an id.
  """
  def get_visit!(%Client{} = client, job_id) do
    job = Scheduling.get_job!(account_scope(client), job_id)

    case job.client_id do
      client_id when client_id == client.id -> job
      _other -> raise Ecto.NoResultsError, queryable: Job
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Reschedules a visit to a new date/start time, preserving its
  original duration, agreed price, and assigned cleaner. Notifies the
  assigned cleaner (and, through their unacknowledged status, the
  office) the same way a staff-driven reschedule does. Refused with
  `{:error, :not_modifiable}` for a completed or already-cancelled
  visit.
  """
  def reschedule_visit(%Client{} = client, %Job{} = job, %{
        "date" => date_input,
        "start_time" => start_time_input
      }) do
    scope = account_scope(client)

    with :ok <- ensure_modifiable(job),
         {:ok, date} <- parse_date(date_input),
         {:ok, start_time} <- parse_time(start_time_input),
         {:ok, updated} <-
           Scheduling.update_job(scope, job, %{
             scheduled_date: date,
             start_time: start_time,
             end_time: shift_end_time(job, start_time)
           }) do
      notify_schedule_change(
        scope,
        updated,
        "Visit rescheduled by the client from #{schedule_label(job)} to #{schedule_label(updated)}"
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  The fee a client would be charged for cancelling `job` right now:
  the account's same-day fee if the visit is scheduled for today, its
  late fee if cancelling inside the notice window, otherwise zero.
  """
  def cancellation_fee_cents(%Client{} = client, %Job{} = job) do
    policy = get_cancellation_policy(client.account_id)
    fee_for(policy, job)
  end

  defp fee_for(%CancellationPolicy{same_day_fee_cents: fee}, %Job{scheduled_date: date})
       when date == ^Date.utc_today() do
    fee
  end

  defp fee_for(%CancellationPolicy{} = policy, %Job{} = job) do
    if hours_until_visit(job) < policy.notice_window_hours do
      policy.late_fee_cents
    else
      0
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Cancels a visit, refusing with `{:error, :not_modifiable}` for one
  already completed or cancelled. Returns the fee charged alongside
  the updated visit — computed against the moment cancellation was
  requested, not looked up again afterward — and notifies the
  assigned cleaner of the cancellation.
  """
  def cancel_visit(%Client{} = client, %Job{} = job) do
    with :ok <- ensure_modifiable(job) do
      scope = account_scope(client)
      fee_cents = cancellation_fee_cents(client, job)

      with {:ok, updated} <- Scheduling.cancel_job(scope, job) do
        notify_schedule_change(scope, updated, "Visit cancelled by the client")
        {:ok, updated, fee_cents}
      end
    end
  end

  ## Cancellation policy

  @doc "The account's cancellation policy, defaulting to a fresh, unsaved (all-zero-fee) one."
  def get_cancellation_policy(account_id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(CancellationPolicy, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> %CancellationPolicy{account_id: account_id}
      policy -> policy
    end
  end

  @doc "Sets (creating or updating) the account's cancellation policy."
  def set_cancellation_policy(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    account_id
    |> get_cancellation_policy()
    |> CancellationPolicy.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
  end

  ## Invoices and payment

  @doc "Every invoice for `client`'s own jobs, most recent first."
  def list_invoices(%Client{} = client) do
    Invoice
    |> join(:inner, [i], j in Job, on: j.id == i.job_id)
    |> where([i, j], j.client_id == ^client.id)
    |> order_by([i], desc: i.inserted_at)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Pays an invoice from the portal: submits the charge (per the
  payments-stripe ADR, this only moves the invoice to
  `:charge_pending` — final `:paid` status is webhook-driven), then
  optionally saves the card on file and records a tip against the
  visit's assigned cleaner.

  `attrs` (string-keyed, straight off the payment form): `"card_token"`
  (required), `"save_card"` (`"true"`/`"on"` to save), `"tip_cents"`
  (blank or omitted to skip the tip).
  """
  def pay_invoice(%Client{} = client, %Invoice{} = invoice, attrs) do
    with {:ok, updated_invoice} <- Billing.pay_via_link(invoice, Map.get(attrs, "card_token")) do
      maybe_save_card(client, attrs)
      maybe_record_tip(updated_invoice, attrs)
      {:ok, updated_invoice}
    end
  end

  defp maybe_save_card(%Client{} = client, %{"save_card" => save_card})
       when save_card in ["true", "on"] do
    Clients.update_client(system_scope(client.account_id), client, %{card_on_file: true})
  end

  defp maybe_save_card(_client, _attrs), do: :ok

  defp maybe_record_tip(%Invoice{} = invoice, attrs) do
    case parse_tip_cents(Map.get(attrs, "tip_cents")) do
      cents when is_integer(cents) and cents > 0 -> record_tip(invoice, cents)
      _no_tip -> :ok
    end
  end

  defp record_tip(%Invoice{} = invoice, cents) do
    %Tip{
      account_id: invoice.account_id,
      invoice_id: invoice.id,
      cleaner_id: invoice.job.cleaner_id
    }
    |> Tip.changeset(%{
      amount_cents: cents,
      stripe_payment_intent_id: invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Cents a cleaner has been tipped through the portal within `period`
  (a `{start_date, end_date}` tuple, matching
  `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.current_pay_period/1`'s own shape) — read
  by `CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.EarningsComponent` to fold tips into a
  cleaner's pay-period total alongside their time-tracked earnings.
  """
  def tip_cents_for_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id, {start_date, end_date})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    start_at = DateTime.new!(start_date, ~T[00:00:00])
    end_at = DateTime.new!(Date.add(end_date, 1), ~T[00:00:00])

    Tip
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and
        t.inserted_at >= ^start_at and t.inserted_at < ^end_at
    )
    |> select([t], sum(t.amount_cents))
    |> Repo.one()
    |> Kernel.||(0)
  end

  ## Shared helpers

  defp account_scope(%Client{account_id: account_id}), do: system_scope(account_id)

  defp system_scope(account_id), do: %Scope{active_account_id: account_id}

  defp ensure_modifiable(%Job{status: status}) when status in [:completed, :cancelled],
    do: {:error, :not_modifiable}

  defp ensure_modifiable(%Job{}), do: :ok

  defp parse_date(%Date{} = date), do: {:ok, date}
  defp parse_date(string) when is_binary(string), do: Date.from_iso8601(string)

  defp parse_time(%Time{} = time), do: {:ok, time}

  defp parse_time(string) when is_binary(string) do
    case String.split(string, ":") do
      [_hour, _minute] -> Time.from_iso8601(string <> ":00")
      _other -> Time.from_iso8601(string)
    end
  end

  defp parse_tip_cents(value) when value in [nil, ""], do: nil

  defp parse_tip_cents(value) when is_binary(value) do
    case Integer.parse(value) do
      {cents, _rest} -> cents
      :error -> nil
    end
  end

  # Moves `start_time` in by the same amount the visit already runs,
  # clamping to end-of-day rather than wrapping past midnight into an
  # earlier clock time — mirrors
  # `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures`' own `default_end_time/1` safeguard.
  defp shift_end_time(%Job{} = job, %Time{} = start_time) do
    {start_seconds, _} = Time.to_seconds_after_midnight(job.start_time)
    {end_seconds, _} = Time.to_seconds_after_midnight(job.end_time)
    candidate = Time.add(start_time, end_seconds - start_seconds, :second)

    if Time.compare(candidate, start_time) == :gt, do: candidate, else: ~T[23:59:59]
  end

  defp hours_until_visit(%Job{scheduled_date: date, start_time: time}) do
    visit_at = DateTime.new!(date, time, "Etc/UTC")
    DateTime.diff(visit_at, DateTime.utc_now(), :hour)
  end

  defp notify_schedule_change(_scope, %Job{cleaner_id: nil}, _summary), do: :ok

  defp notify_schedule_change(scope, %Job{} = job, summary) do
    Notifications.create_notification(scope, %{
      cleaner_id: job.cleaner_id,
      job_id: job.id,
      kind: :schedule_change,
      channel: :push,
      status: :pending,
      change_summary: summary,
      pushed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
      token: "portal_schedule_change_#{job.id}_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
    })
  end

  defp schedule_label(%Job{} = job),
    do: "#{job.scheduled_date} #{format_time_12h(job.start_time)}-#{format_time_12h(job.end_time)}"

  defp format_time_12h(%Time{} = time) do
    {hour, period} = to_12_hour(time.hour)
    minute = time.minute |> Integer.to_string() |> String.pad_leading(2, "0")
    "#{hour}:#{minute} #{period}"
  end

  defp to_12_hour(0), do: {12, "AM"}
  defp to_12_hour(hour) when hour < 12, do: {hour, "AM"}
  defp to_12_hour(12), do: {12, "PM"}
  defp to_12_hour(hour), do: {hour - 12, "PM"}
end

  Pays an invoice from the portal: submits the charge (per the
  payments-stripe ADR, this only moves the invoice to
  `:charge_pending` — final `:paid` status is webhook-driven), then
  optionally saves the card on file and records a tip against the
  visit's assigned cleaner.

  `attrs` (string-keyed, straight off the payment form): `"card_token"`
  (required), `"save_card"` (`"true"`/`"on"` to save), `"tip_cents"`
  (blank or omitted to skip the tip).
  """
  def pay_invoice(%Client{} = client, %Invoice{} = invoice, attrs) do
    with {:ok, updated_invoice} <- Billing.pay_via_link(invoice, Map.get(attrs, "card_token")) do
      maybe_save_card(client, attrs)
      maybe_record_tip(updated_invoice, attrs)
      {:ok, updated_invoice}
    end
  end

  defp maybe_save_card(%Client{} = client, %{"save_card" => save_card})
       when save_card in ["true", "on"] do
    Clients.update_client(system_scope(client.account_id), client, %{card_on_file: true})
  end

  defp maybe_save_card(_client, _attrs), do: :ok

  defp maybe_record_tip(%Invoice{} = invoice, attrs) do
    case parse_tip_cents(Map.get(attrs, "tip_cents")) do
      cents when is_integer(cents) and cents > 0 -> record_tip(invoice, cents)
      _no_tip -> :ok
    end
  end

  defp record_tip(%Invoice{} = invoice, cents) do
    %Tip{
      account_id: invoice.account_id,
      invoice_id: invoice.id,
      cleaner_id: invoice.job.cleaner_id
    }
    |> Tip.changeset(%{
      amount_cents: cents,
      stripe_payment_intent_id: invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Cents a cleaner has been tipped through the portal within `period`
  (a `{start_date, end_date}` tuple, matching
  `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.current_pay_period/1`'s own shape) — read
  by `CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.EarningsComponent` to fold tips into a
  cleaner's pay-period total alongside their time-tracked earnings.
  """
  def tip_cents_for_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id, {start_date, end_date})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    start_at = DateTime.new!(start_date, ~T[00:00:00])
    end_at = DateTime.new!(Date.add(end_date, 1), ~T[00:00:00])

    Tip
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and
        t.inserted_at >= ^start_at and t.inserted_at < ^end_at
    )
    |> select([t], sum(t.amount_cents))
    |> Repo.one()
    |> Kernel.||(0)
  end

  ## Shared helpers

  defp account_scope(%Client{account_id: account_id}), do: system_scope(account_id)

  defp system_scope(account_id), do: %Scope{active_account_id: account_id}

  defp ensure_modifiable(%Job{status: status}) when status in [:completed, :cancelled],
    do: {:error, :not_modifiable}

  defp ensure_modifiable(%Job{}), do: :ok

  defp parse_date(%Date{} = date), do: {:ok, date}
  defp parse_date(string) when is_binary(string), do: Date.from_iso8601(string)

  defp parse_time(%Time{} = time), do: {:ok, time}

  defp parse_time(string) when is_binary(string) do
    case String.split(string, ":") do
      [_hour, _minute] -> Time.from_iso8601(string <> ":00")
      _other -> Time.from_iso8601(string)
    end
  end

  defp parse_tip_cents(value) when value in [nil, ""], do: nil

  defp parse_tip_cents(value) when is_binary(value) do
    case Integer.parse(value) do
      {cents, _rest} -> cents
      :error -> nil
    end
  end

  # Moves `start_time` in by the same amount the visit already runs,
  # clamping to end-of-day rather than wrapping past midnight into an
  # earlier clock time — mirrors
  # `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures`' own `default_end_time/1` safeguard.
  defp shift_end_time(%Job{} = job, %Time{} = start_time) do
    {start_seconds, _} = Time.to_seconds_after_midnight(job.start_time)
    {end_seconds, _} = Time.to_seconds_after_midnight(job.end_time)
    candidate = Time.add(start_time, end_seconds - start_seconds, :second)

    if Time.compare(candidate, start_time) == :gt, do: candidate, else: ~T[23:59:59]
  end

  defp hours_until_visit(%Job{scheduled_date: date, start_time: time}) do
    visit_at = DateTime.new!(date, time, "Etc/UTC")
    DateTime.diff(visit_at, DateTime.utc_now(), :hour)
  end

  defp notify_schedule_change(_scope, %Job{cleaner_id: nil}, _summary), do: :ok

  defp notify_schedule_change(scope, %Job{} = job, summary) do
    Notifications.create_notification(scope, %{
      cleaner_id: job.cleaner_id,
      job_id: job.id,
      kind: :schedule_change,
      channel: :push,
      status: :pending,
      change_summary: summary,
      pushed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
      token: "portal_schedule_change_#{job.id}_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
    })
  end

  defp schedule_label(%Job{} = job),
    do: "#{job.scheduled_date} #{format_time_12h(job.start_time)}-#{format_time_12h(job.end_time)}"

  defp format_time_12h(%Time{} = time) do
    {hour, period} = to_12_hour(time.hour)
    minute = time.minute |> Integer.to_string() |> String.pad_leading(2, "0")
    "#{hour}:#{minute} #{period}"
  end

  defp to_12_hour(0), do: {12, "AM"}
  defp to_12_hour(hour) when hour < 12, do: {hour, "AM"}
  defp to_12_hour(12), do: {12, "PM"}
  defp to_12_hour(hour), do: {hour - 12, "PM"}
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth do
  @moduledoc """
  Gates the client portal's LiveViews behind a magic-link session —
  no user login. Reads the client id `CleanerCrmWeb.PortalController`
  wrote to the session's `:portal_client_id` key after a valid
  `/portal/access/:token` exchange, mirroring how
  `CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth` reads `:user_token` for staff auth.

  ## Usage

      live_session :portal,
        on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth, :require_client}] do
        live "/portal", PortalLive.Home, :index
      end
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

  alias CleanerCrm.Portal

  def on_mount(:require_client, _params, session, socket) do
    case session["portal_client_id"] do
      nil ->
        socket =
          socket
          |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "Please use your portal link to sign in.")
          |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/")

        {:halt, socket}

      client_id ->
        {:cont, Phoenix.Component.assign_new(socket, :client, fn -> Portal.get_client!(client_id) end)}
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PortalController do
  @moduledoc """
  The magic-link entry point into the client portal: `GET
  /portal/access/:token` exchanges a token (mailed to the client, or
  handed out at booking) for a portal session — no password
  required.

  ## Dependencies

  - `CleanerCrm.Portal`
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Portal

  def access(conn, %{"token" => token}) do
    case Portal.access_portal(token) do
      {:ok, client_id} ->
        conn
        |> put_session(:portal_client_id, client_id)
        |> redirect(to: ~p"/portal")

      {:error, :invalid} ->
        render(conn, :invalid)
    end
  end
end

This pay period
{Money.format_cents(@total_cents)}

Drive time between jobs is {drive_time_label(@drive_time_policy)}.

""" end @impl true def update(assigns, socket) do scope = assigns.current_scope period = TimeTracking.current_pay_period(scope) totals = TimeTracking.cleaner_pay_totals(scope, period) {:ok, socket |> assign(assigns) |> assign(:total_cents, Map.get(totals, scope.user.id, 0)) |> assign(:drive_time_policy, TimeTracking.drive_time_policy(scope))} end defp drive_time_label(:paid), do: "paid" defp drive_time_label(:unpaid), do: "unpaid" end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # No `:protect_from_forgery` — unlike the GET-only public routes below
  # (which can just use `:browser`), `/pay/:token` accepts a POST from a
  # client with no session and no CSRF token (a mailed or shared link).
  # `:fetch_current_scope_for_user` still runs — the root layout reads
  # `@current_scope` unconditionally, and this plug assigns `nil` when
  # no one's logged in rather than requiring an authenticated visitor.
  pipeline :public do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :webhook do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # Office-only controller routes (e.g. the payroll CSV export) layer
  # this on top of `:require_authenticated_user`; office-only
  # LiveViews use the equivalent `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole`
  # on_mount hook instead, since a plug can't gate a live_session.
  pipeline :require_office_role do
    plug CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index

      live "/field", FieldLive.Today, :index
      live "/field/jobs/:id", FieldLive.Job, :show
    end

    # Office-only surfaces: dispatch, payroll, quality, invoicing,
    # clients, quotes, reminders, and the audit trail. Gated to
    # owners/admins by `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole` — a cleaner
    # is redirected to `/field` instead. See that module for why it's
    # a separate `live_session` from the one above.
    live_session :require_office_role,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
      ] do
      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new

      live "/audit", AuditLive, :index

      live "/quotes", QuoteLive.Index, :index
      live "/quotes/new", QuoteLive.Builder, :new
      live "/quotes/:id", QuoteLive.Builder, :show

      live "/quality", QualityLive.Review, :index
      live "/quality/scorecards", QualityLive.Scorecards, :index
      live "/quality/templates", QualityLive.Templates, :index
      live "/quality/templates/new", QualityLive.Templates, :new
      live "/quality/templates/:id/edit", QualityLive.Templates, :edit
      live "/quality/:job_id", QualityLive.Review, :show

      live "/timesheets", TimesheetLive, :index

      live "/invoices", InvoiceLive.Index, :index
      live "/invoices/:id", InvoiceLive.Show, :show

      live "/reminders", ReminderLive, :index
    end

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user, :require_office_role]

    get "/timesheets/export", TimesheetExportController, :show
  end

  scope "/integrations/oauth", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
    get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new
      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete

    # Public confirm/reschedule links a client reaches from their
    # reminder — no login, so `:browser` (not `:require_authenticated_user`)
    # like the routes above. Plain `:browser`, not `:public`, so
    # `fetch_current_scope_for_user` still assigns `current_scope` for
    # the root layout.
    get "/reminders/confirm/:token", ReminderController, :confirm
    get "/reminders/reschedule/:token", ReminderController, :reschedule
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :public

    get "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :show
    post "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :create
  end

  scope "/webhooks", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :webhook

    post "/stripe", StripeWebhookController, :create
    post "/twilio", TwilioWebhookController, :status
  end
end

@impl true
  def update(assigns, socket) do
    scope = assigns.current_scope
    period = TimeTracking.current_pay_period(scope)
    totals = TimeTracking.cleaner_pay_totals(scope, period)
    time_tracked_cents = Map.get(totals, scope.user.id, 0)

    {:ok,
     socket
     |> assign(assigns)
     |> assign(:total_cents, time_tracked_cents + portal_tip_cents(scope, period))
     |> assign(:drive_time_policy, TimeTracking.drive_time_policy(scope))}
  end

  # `CleanerCrm.Portal` (story 852) may not exist yet, or may land
  # after this component does — read defensively
  # (`Code.ensure_loaded?/1` + `function_exported?/3`), mirroring
  # `FieldLive.Today`'s optional read of `CleanerCrm.Notifications`.
  # Expected contract: `tip_cents_for_cleaner/3` sums the cents a
  # cleaner has been tipped through the portal within the given pay
  # period.
  defp portal_tip_cents(scope, period) do
    if Code.ensure_loaded?(CleanerCrm.Portal) and
         function_exported?(CleanerCrm.Portal, :tip_cents_for_cleaner, 3) do
      CleanerCrm.Portal.tip_cents_for_cleaner(scope, scope.user.id, period)
    else
      0
    end
  end

  defp drive_time_label(:paid), do: "paid"
  defp drive_time_label(:unpaid), do: "unpaid"
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # No `:protect_from_forgery` — unlike the GET-only public routes below
  # (which can just use `:browser`), `/pay/:token` accepts a POST from a
  # client with no session and no CSRF token (a mailed or shared link).
  # `:fetch_current_scope_for_user` still runs — the root layout reads
  # `@current_scope` unconditionally, and this plug assigns `nil` when
  # no one's logged in rather than requiring an authenticated visitor.
  pipeline :public do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :webhook do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # Office-only controller routes (e.g. the payroll CSV export) layer
  # this on top of `:require_authenticated_user`; office-only
  # LiveViews use the equivalent `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole`
  # on_mount hook instead, since a plug can't gate a live_session.
  pipeline :require_office_role do
    plug CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index

      live "/field", FieldLive.Today, :index
      live "/field/jobs/:id", FieldLive.Job, :show
    end

    # Office-only surfaces: dispatch, payroll, quality, invoicing,
    # clients, quotes, reminders, and the audit trail. Gated to
    # owners/admins by `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole` — a cleaner
    # is redirected to `/field` instead. See that module for why it's
    # a separate `live_session` from the one above.
    live_session :require_office_role,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
      ] do
      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new

      live "/audit", AuditLive, :index

      live "/quotes", QuoteLive.Index, :index
      live "/quotes/new", QuoteLive.Builder, :new
      live "/quotes/:id", QuoteLive.Builder, :show

      live "/quality", QualityLive.Review, :index
      live "/quality/scorecards", QualityLive.Scorecards, :index
      live "/quality/templates", QualityLive.Templates, :index
      live "/quality/templates/new", QualityLive.Templates, :new
      live "/quality/templates/:id/edit", QualityLive.Templates, :edit
      live "/quality/:job_id", QualityLive.Review, :show

      live "/timesheets", TimesheetLive, :index

      live "/invoices", InvoiceLive.Index, :index
      live "/invoices/:id", InvoiceLive.Show, :show

      live "/reminders", ReminderLive, :index
    end

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user, :require_office_role]

    get "/timesheets/export", TimesheetExportController, :show
  end

  scope "/integrations/oauth", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
    get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new
      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete

    # Public confirm/reschedule links a client reaches from their
    # reminder — no login, so `:browser` (not `:require_authenticated_user`)
    # like the routes above. Plain `:browser`, not `:public`, so
    # `fetch_current_scope_for_user` still assigns `current_scope` for
    # the root layout.
    get "/reminders/confirm/:token", ReminderController, :confirm
    get "/reminders/reschedule/:token", ReminderController, :reschedule
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :public

    get "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :show
    post "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :create
  end

  scope "/webhooks", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :webhook

    post "/stripe", StripeWebhookController, :create
    post "/twilio", TwilioWebhookController, :status
  end

  # Reviews (story 853): the public token-link review page needs no
  # login — mirrors `/invitations/accept/:token`'s `:current_user`
  # live_session so `current_scope` still mounts for the root layout —
  # while the owner's review inbox is office-only, gated the same way
  # as the other office surfaces above.
  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :reviews_public,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/reviews/:token", ReviewLive.Public, :show
    end
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :reviews_office,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
      ] do
      live "/reviews", ReviewLive.Index, :index
    end
  end
end

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index

      live "/field", FieldLive.Today, :index
      live "/field/jobs/:id", FieldLive.Job, :show
    end

    # Office-only surfaces: dispatch, payroll, quality, invoicing,
    # clients, quotes, reminders, and the audit trail. Gated to
    # owners/admins by `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole` — a cleaner
    # is redirected to `/field` instead. See that module for why it's
    # a separate `live_session` from the one above.
    live_session :require_office_role,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
      ] do
      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new

      live "/audit", AuditLive, :index

      live "/quotes", QuoteLive.Index, :index
      live "/quotes/new", QuoteLive.Builder, :new
      live "/quotes/:id", QuoteLive.Builder, :show

      live "/quality", QualityLive.Review, :index
      live "/quality/scorecards", QualityLive.Scorecards, :index
      live "/quality/templates", QualityLive.Templates, :index
      live "/quality/templates/new", QualityLive.Templates, :new
      live "/quality/templates/:id/edit", QualityLive.Templates, :edit
      live "/quality/:job_id", QualityLive.Review, :show

      live "/timesheets", TimesheetLive, :index

      live "/invoices", InvoiceLive.Index, :index
      live "/invoices/:id", InvoiceLive.Show, :show

      live "/reminders", ReminderLive, :index
    end

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user, :require_office_role]

    get "/timesheets/export", TimesheetExportController, :show
  end

  scope "/integrations/oauth", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
    get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new
      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete

    # Public confirm/reschedule links a client reaches from their
    # reminder — no login, so `:browser` (not `:require_authenticated_user`)
    # like the routes above. Plain `:browser`, not `:public`, so
    # `fetch_current_scope_for_user` still assigns `current_scope` for
    # the root layout.
    get "/reminders/confirm/:token", ReminderController, :confirm
    get "/reminders/reschedule/:token", ReminderController, :reschedule
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :public

    get "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :show
    post "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :create
  end

  scope "/webhooks", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :webhook

    post "/stripe", StripeWebhookController, :create
    post "/twilio", TwilioWebhookController, :status
  end

  # Reviews (story 853): the public token-link review page needs no
  # login — mirrors `/invitations/accept/:token`'s `:current_user`
  # live_session so `current_scope` still mounts for the root layout —
  # while the owner's review inbox is office-only, gated the same way
  # as the other office surfaces above.
  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :reviews_public,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/reviews/:token", ReviewLive.Public, :show
    end
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :reviews_office,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
      ] do
      live "/reviews", ReviewLive.Index, :index
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Reviews.ReviewTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.DataCase, async: true

  alias CleanerCrm.Reviews.Review

  @valid_attrs %{
    job_id: Ecto.UUID.generate(),
    client_id: Ecto.UUID.generate(),
    token: "review_token_123",
    status: :review_requested,
    review_request_sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
  }

  describe "changeset/2" do
    test "valid with just the request-side fields, no rating yet" do
      changeset = Review.changeset(%Review{}, @valid_attrs)
      assert changeset.valid?
    end

    test "requires job_id, client_id, and token" do
      changeset = Review.changeset(%Review{}, %{})
      refute changeset.valid?

      assert %{job_id: ["can't be blank"], client_id: ["can't be blank"], token: ["can't be blank"]} =
               errors_on(changeset)
    end

    test "rejects a rating outside 1..5" do
      changeset = Review.changeset(%Review{}, Map.put(@valid_attrs, :rating, 6))
      refute changeset.valid?
      assert %{rating: ["is invalid"]} = errors_on(changeset)
    end
  end

  describe "submission_changeset/2" do
    test "valid with a rating, text, status, and submitted_at" do
      changeset =
        Review.submission_changeset(%Review{}, %{
          rating: 5,
          text: "Great job!",
          status: :published,
          submitted_at: DateTime.utc_now()
        })

      assert changeset.valid?
    end

    test "requires rating and submitted_at" do
      changeset = Review.submission_changeset(%Review{}, %{})
      refute changeset.valid?
      assert %{rating: ["can't be blank"], submitted_at: ["can't be blank"]} = errors_on(changeset)
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.BillingTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.DataCase, async: true

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Billing
  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.Invoice
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  setup do
    owner = user_fixture()
    owner_scope = Scope.for_user(owner)
    {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(owner_scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co"})
    scope = %{owner_scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}

    {:ok, client} = Clients.create_client(scope, %{name: "A Client"})

    %{scope: scope, client: client}
  end

  defp job_fixture(scope, client, attrs) do
    {:ok, job} =
      Scheduling.create_job(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          scheduled_date: Date.utc_today(),
          start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
          status: :scheduled
        })
      )

    job
  end

  describe "generate_for_job/2" do
    test "generates an invoice for the job's agreed price", %{scope: scope, client: client} do
      job = job_fixture(scope, client, %{agreed_price_cents: 15_000})

      assert {:ok, %Invoice{} = invoice} = Billing.generate_for_job(scope, job)
      assert invoice.amount_cents == 15_000
      assert invoice.job_id == job.id
    end

    # Regression: a job materialized from a recurring plan with no price
    # (e.g. `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence.job_attrs/1` on an unpriced
    # plan) has `agreed_price_cents: nil`. Generating its invoice used to
    # attempt an insert with a `nil` `amount_cents` and crash on the
    # column's NOT NULL constraint — completing the job must still
    # succeed, so this must return an error tuple, never raise.
    test "skips invoice creation and returns {:error, :no_price} for a nil-priced job, without touching the database",
         %{scope: scope, client: client} do
      job = job_fixture(scope, client, %{agreed_price_cents: nil})

      assert {:error, :no_price} = Billing.generate_for_job(scope, job)
      assert Billing.list_invoices(scope) == []
    end
  end

  describe "create_invoice/2" do
    test "refuses a nil amount_cents with a changeset error instead of crashing", %{
      scope: scope,
      client: client
    } do
      job = job_fixture(scope, client, %{agreed_price_cents: nil})

      assert {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} =
               Billing.create_invoice(scope, %{job_id: job.id, status: :unpaid})

      assert %{amount_cents: ["can't be blank"]} = errors_on(changeset)
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Portal.PortalSessionTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.DataCase, async: true

  alias CleanerCrm.Portal.PortalSession

  @client %{id: Ecto.UUID.generate(), account_id: Ecto.UUID.generate()}

  describe "build_changeset/2" do
    test "is valid and carries a plaintext token alongside its hash" do
      changeset = PortalSession.build_changeset(@client, %{})

      assert changeset.valid?
      assert token = get_change(changeset, :token)
      assert is_binary(token)
      assert get_change(changeset, :token_hash) == PortalSession.hash_token(token)
    end

    test "scopes the session to the given client and account" do
      changeset = PortalSession.build_changeset(@client, %{})

      assert changeset.data.client_id == @client.id
      assert changeset.data.account_id == @client.account_id
    end

    test "defaults expires_at several days out when not given" do
      changeset = PortalSession.build_changeset(@client, %{})

      assert %DateTime{} = expires_at = get_change(changeset, :expires_at)
      assert DateTime.compare(expires_at, DateTime.utc_now()) == :gt
    end

    test "honors an explicit expires_at override" do
      expires_at = DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), -3600, :second)
      changeset = PortalSession.build_changeset(@client, %{expires_at: expires_at})

      assert get_change(changeset, :expires_at) == expires_at
    end
  end

  describe "hash_token/1" do
    test "is deterministic for the same input" do
      assert PortalSession.hash_token("abc") == PortalSession.hash_token("abc")
    end

    test "differs for different inputs" do
      refute PortalSession.hash_token("abc") == PortalSession.hash_token("xyz")
    end
  end

  describe "expired?/1" do
    test "false for a session expiring in the future" do
      session = %PortalSession{expires_at: DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), 3600, :second)}
      refute PortalSession.expired?(session)
    end

    test "true for a session that already expired" do
      session = %PortalSession{expires_at: DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), -3600, :second)}
      assert PortalSession.expired?(session)
    end
  end

  describe "touch_changeset/1" do
    test "stamps last_used_at to now" do
      changeset = PortalSession.touch_changeset(%PortalSession{})

      assert %DateTime{} = last_used_at = get_change(changeset, :last_used_at)
      assert DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(), last_used_at, :second) < 5
    end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Portal.PortalSessionTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.DataCase, async: true

  alias CleanerCrm.Portal.PortalSession

  @client %{id: Ecto.UUID.generate(), account_id: Ecto.UUID.generate()}

  describe "build_changeset/2" do
    test "is valid and carries a plaintext token alongside its hash" do
      changeset = PortalSession.build_changeset(@client, %{})

      assert changeset.valid?
      assert token = get_change(changeset, :token)
      assert is_binary(token)
      assert get_change(changeset, :token_hash) == PortalSession.hash_token(token)
    end

    test "scopes the session to the given client and account" do
      changeset = PortalSession.build_changeset(@client, %{})

      assert changeset.data.client_id == @client.id
      assert changeset.data.account_id == @client.account_id
    end

    test "defaults expires_at several days out when not given" do
      changeset = PortalSession.build_changeset(@client, %{})

      assert %DateTime{} = expires_at = get_change(changeset, :expires_at)
      assert DateTime.compare(expires_at, DateTime.utc_now()) == :gt
    end

    test "honors an explicit expires_at override" do
      expires_at = DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), -3600, :second)
      changeset = PortalSession.build_changeset(@client, %{expires_at: expires_at})

      assert get_change(changeset, :expires_at) == expires_at
    end
  end

  describe "hash_token/1" do
    test "is deterministic for the same input" do
      assert PortalSession.hash_token("abc") == PortalSession.hash_token("abc")
    end

    test "differs for different inputs" do
      refute PortalSession.hash_token("abc") == PortalSession.hash_token("xyz")
    end
  end

  describe "expired?/1" do
    test "false for a session expiring in the future" do
      session = %PortalSession{expires_at: DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), 3600, :second)}
      refute PortalSession.expired?(session)
    end

    test "true for a session that already expired" do
      session = %PortalSession{expires_at: DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), -3600, :second)}
      assert PortalSession.expired?(session)
    end
  end

  describe "touch_changeset/1" do
    test "stamps last_used_at to now" do
      changeset = PortalSession.touch_changeset(%PortalSession{})

      assert %DateTime{} = last_used_at = get_change(changeset, :last_used_at)
      assert DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(), last_used_at, :second) < 5
    end
  end
end

    end

    test "rejects a negative notice window" do

        CancellationPolicy.changeset(%CancellationPolicy{}, %{@valid_attrs | notice_window_hours: -1})

        )

      assert changeset.valid?
