defmodule CleanerCrm.PortalTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.DataCase, async: true

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Billing
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients
  alias CleanerCrm.Portal
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  setup do
    owner = user_fixture()
    owner_scope = Scope.for_user(owner)
    {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(owner_scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co"})
    scope = %{owner_scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}

    {:ok, client} = Clients.create_client(scope, %{name: "A Client"})

    %{scope: scope, account: account, client: client}
  end

  defp job_fixture(scope, client, attrs) do
    {:ok, job} =
      Scheduling.create_job(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),
          start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
          status: :scheduled
        })
      )

    job
  end

  describe "create_portal_session/2 and access_portal/1" do
    test "a fresh token grants access to the client that issued it", %{client: client} do
      {:ok, session} = Portal.create_portal_session(client, %{})

      assert {:ok, client_id} = Portal.access_portal(session.token)
      assert client_id == client.id
    end

    test "an expired token is refused" do
      {:ok, client} = Clients.create_client(user_fixture() |> Scope.for_user(), %{name: "X"})
      flunk_if_no_account = client
      _ = flunk_if_no_account
    end
  end

  describe "access_portal/1 failure paths" do
    test "an expired session is refused", %{client: client} do
      {:ok, session} =
        Portal.create_portal_session(client, %{
          expires_at: DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), -3600, :second)
        })

      assert {:error, :invalid} = Portal.access_portal(session.token)
    end

    test "an unknown token is refused" do
      assert {:error, :invalid} = Portal.access_portal("not-a-real-token")
    end
  end

  describe "list_upcoming_visits/1 and list_visit_history/1" do
    test "upcoming visits excludes completed and cancelled jobs", %{scope: scope, client: client} do
      upcoming = job_fixture(scope, client, %{})
      completed = job_fixture(scope, client, %{status: :completed})
      {:ok, cancelled} = Scheduling.cancel_job(scope, job_fixture(scope, client, %{}))

      visits = Portal.list_upcoming_visits(client)

      assert Enum.map(visits, & &1.id) == [upcoming.id]
      refute Enum.any?(visits, &(&1.id == completed.id))
      refute Enum.any?(visits, &(&1.id == cancelled.id))
    end

    test "visit history only includes completed jobs", %{scope: scope, client: client} do
      job_fixture(scope, client, %{})
      completed = job_fixture(scope, client, %{status: :completed})

      history = Portal.list_visit_history(client)

      assert Enum.map(history, & &1.id) == [completed.id]
    end
  end

  describe "get_visit!/2" do
    test "fetches a visit belonging to the client", %{scope: scope, client: client} do
      job = job_fixture(scope, client, %{})

      assert Portal.get_visit!(client, job.id).id == job.id
    end

    test "raises when the job belongs to a different client", %{scope: scope, client: client} do
      {:ok, other_client} = Clients.create_client(scope, %{name: "Someone Else"})
      job = job_fixture(scope, other_client, %{})

      assert_raise Ecto.NoResultsError, fn -> Portal.get_visit!(client, job.id) end
    end
  end

  describe "reschedule_visit/3" do
    test "moves the date/time while preserving price and cleaner", %{
      scope: scope,
      account: account,
      client: client
    } do
      cleaner = CleanerCrm.SchedulingFixtures.cleaner_fixture(scope, account)

      job =
        job_fixture(scope, client, %{
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          agreed_price_cents: 15_000,
          start_time: ~T[10:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[12:00:00]
        })

      new_date = Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10)

      assert {:ok, updated} =
               Portal.reschedule_visit(client, job, %{
                 "date" => Date.to_iso8601(new_date),
                 "start_time" => "14:00"
               })

      assert updated.scheduled_date == new_date
      assert updated.start_time == ~T[14:00:00]
      assert updated.end_time == ~T[16:00:00]
      assert updated.agreed_price_cents == 15_000
      assert updated.cleaner_id == cleaner.id
    end

    test "refuses to reschedule a completed visit", %{scope: scope, client: client} do
      job = job_fixture(scope, client, %{status: :completed})

      assert {:error, :not_modifiable} =
               Portal.reschedule_visit(client, job, %{
                 "date" => Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10)),
                 "start_time" => "14:00"
               })
    end
  end

  describe "cancellation_fee_cents/2 and cancel_visit/2" do
    setup %{scope: scope} do
      {:ok, _policy} =
        Portal.set_cancellation_policy(scope, %{
          notice_window_hours: 48,
          late_fee_cents: 2_500,
          same_day_fee_cents: 5_000
        })

      :ok
    end

    test "no fee outside the notice window", %{scope: scope, client: client} do
      job = job_fixture(scope, client, %{scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 5)})
      assert Portal.cancellation_fee_cents(client, job) == 0
    end

    test "the late fee inside the notice window", %{scope: scope, client: client} do
      job =
        job_fixture(scope, client, %{
          scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 1),
          start_time: ~T[10:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[12:00:00]
        })

      assert Portal.cancellation_fee_cents(client, job) == 2_500
    end

    test "the maximum fee for a same-day cancellation", %{scope: scope, client: client} do
      job =
        job_fixture(scope, client, %{
          scheduled_date: Date.utc_today(),
          start_time: ~T[18:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[20:00:00]
        })

      assert Portal.cancellation_fee_cents(client, job) == 5_000
    end

    test "cancels the visit and reports the fee charged", %{scope: scope, client: client} do
      job =
        job_fixture(scope, client, %{
          scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 1),
          start_time: ~T[10:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[12:00:00]
        })

      assert {:ok, updated, 2_500} = Portal.cancel_visit(client, job)
      assert updated.status == :cancelled
    end

    test "refuses to cancel an already-cancelled visit", %{scope: scope, client: client} do
      job = job_fixture(scope, client, %{})
      {:ok, _updated, _fee} = Portal.cancel_visit(client, job)

      assert {:error, :not_modifiable} = Portal.cancel_visit(client, %{job | status: :cancelled})
    end
  end

  describe "get_cancellation_policy/1" do
    test "defaults to a 24-hour window with no fees when unset", %{account: account} do
      policy = Portal.get_cancellation_policy(account.id)

      assert policy.notice_window_hours == 24
      assert policy.late_fee_cents == 0
      assert policy.same_day_fee_cents == 0
    end
  end

  describe "invoices and payment" do
    setup %{scope: scope, client: client} do
      job = job_fixture(scope, client, %{status: :completed, agreed_price_cents: 15_000})
      {:ok, invoice} = Billing.create_invoice(scope, %{job_id: job.id, amount_cents: 15_000})
      %{job: job, invoice: invoice}
    end

    test "lists only this client's invoices", %{scope: scope, client: client, invoice: invoice} do
      {:ok, other_client} = Clients.create_client(scope, %{name: "Someone Else"})
      other_job = job_fixture(scope, other_client, %{status: :completed})
      {:ok, _other_invoice} = Billing.create_invoice(scope, %{job_id: other_job.id, amount_cents: 1})

      invoices = Portal.list_invoices(client)

      assert Enum.map(invoices, & &1.id) == [invoice.id]
    end

    test "pays an invoice, saves the card, and records a tip for the assigned cleaner", %{
      scope: scope,
      account: account,
      client: client,
      job: job,
      invoice: invoice
    } do
      cleaner = CleanerCrm.SchedulingFixtures.cleaner_fixture(scope, account)
      {:ok, job} = Scheduling.assign_cleaner(scope, job, cleaner.id)
      invoice = %{invoice | job: job}

      assert {:ok, updated_invoice} =
               Portal.pay_invoice(client, invoice, %{

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.ChecklistComponentTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.ClientsFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Billing
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  defp owner_scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{user: user, scope: %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}}
  end

  # Regression for the accepted issue: completing a job with no agreed
  # price crashed invoice generation on the `invoices.amount_cents` NOT
  # NULL constraint. An unpriced recurring plan materializes visits
  # with no price (`CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence.job_attrs/1`), so
  # this drives that exact real-usage path end to end: create such a
  # plan, then complete the job it generated through the live UI.
  test "completing a plan-generated job with no agreed price completes without crashing and skips its invoice" do
    %{user: owner, scope: scope} = owner_scope_fixture()
    client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Jamie Rivera"})
    property = property_fixture(scope, client)

    {:ok, {_plan, [job]}} =
      Scheduling.create_recurring_plan(scope, %{
        property_id: property.id,
        recurrence: :weekly,
        start_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),
        occurrence_count: 1
      })

    refute job.agreed_price_cents

    conn = log_in_user(build_conn(), owner)
    {:ok, job_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{job.id}")

    job_live
    |> element("[data-test='mark-complete-button']")
    |> render_click()

    # `ChecklistComponent`'s `send(self(), :job_completed)` lands in the
    # LiveView's mailbox after the click's own render returns — matching
    # story 836's own criterion 7153 spec, a fresh `render/1` is needed
    # to observe the follow-up reload it triggers.
    assert render(job_live) =~ "Complete"

    assert Scheduling.get_job!(scope, job.id).status == :completed
    assert Billing.list_invoices(scope) == []
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PortalLive.HomeTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.ClientsFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Quality
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  defp owner_scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)
    {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co"})
    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp portal_conn(client) do
    build_conn()
    |> init_test_session(%{})
    |> put_session(:portal_client_id, client.id)
  end

  test "shows an upcoming visit's assigned cleaner and a completed visit's proof-of-work" do
    scope = owner_scope_fixture()
    client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Morgan Blake"})

    cleaner = CleanerCrm.SchedulingFixtures.cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)

    upcoming =
      Scheduling.create_job(scope, %{
        client_id: client.id,
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),
        start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
      })
      |> then(fn {:ok, job} -> job end)

    {:ok, completed} =
      Scheduling.create_job(scope, %{
        client_id: client.id,
        scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), -7),
        start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
        status: :completed
      })

    {:ok, _checklist} =
      Quality.complete_checklist(scope, completed, [
        %{task: "Kitchen counters wiped down", before_photo: "before.jpg", after_photo: "after.jpg"}
      ])

    {:ok, portal_live, _html} = live(portal_conn(client), ~p"/portal")

    assert has_element?(portal_live, "[data-test='upcoming-visits']")
    assert has_element?(portal_live, "[data-test='visit-#{upcoming.id}']", cleaner.name)

    assert has_element?(
             portal_live,
             "[data-test='service-history'] [data-test='visit-#{completed.id}']",
             "Kitchen counters wiped down"
           )

    assert has_element?(
             portal_live,
             "[data-test='visit-#{completed.id}'] [data-test='before-photo']"
           )
  end

  test "an unassigned upcoming visit shows a placeholder instead of a cleaner" do
    scope = owner_scope_fixture()
    client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Morgan Blake"})

    {:ok, job} =
      Scheduling.create_job(scope, %{
        client_id: client.id,
        scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),
        start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
      })

    {:ok, portal_live, _html} = live(portal_conn(client), ~p"/portal")

    assert has_element?(
             portal_live,
             "[data-test='visit-#{job.id}'] [data-test='cleaner-not-assigned']"
           )
  end

  test "redirects home when there is no portal session" do
    assert {:error, {:redirect, %{to: "/"}}} = live(build_conn(), ~p"/portal")
  end
end

  alias CleanerCrm.Portal

    client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Morgan Blake"})

    {:ok, job} =
      Scheduling.create_job(scope, %{
        client_id: client.id,
        agreed_price_cents: 15_000,
        scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),

    |> form("[data-test='reschedule-form']",

      Scheduling.create_job(scope, %{
        client_id: client.id,
        scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 1),
        start_time: ~T[10:00:00],

        end_time: ~T[11:00:00],

      })

    job

    paid_job = completed_job_fixture(scope, client)
    {:ok, paid} = Billing.create_invoice(scope, %{job_id: paid_job.id, amount_cents: 15_000, status: :paid})

    unpaid_job = completed_job_fixture(scope, client)

    {:ok, invoices_live, _html} = live(portal_conn(client), ~p"/portal/invoices")

    assert has_element?(invoices_live, "[data-test='invoice-row-#{unpaid.id}']", "Unpaid")
  end

    client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Morgan Blake", card_on_file: false})
    job = completed_job_fixture(scope, client)

defmodule CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures do
  @moduledoc """
  This module defines test helpers for creating
  entities via the `CleanerCrm.Users` context.
  """

  import Ecto.Query

  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  def unique_user_email, do: "user#{System.unique_integer()}@example.com"
  def valid_user_password, do: "hello world!"

  def valid_user_attributes(attrs \\ %{}) do
    Enum.into(attrs, %{
      email: unique_user_email()
    })
  end

  def unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, user} =
      attrs
      |> valid_user_attributes()
      |> Users.register_user()

    user
  end

  def user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}) do
    user = unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs)

    token =
      extract_user_token(fn url ->
        Users.deliver_login_instructions(user, url)
      end)

    {:ok, {user, _expired_tokens}} =
      Users.login_user_by_magic_link(token)

    user
  end

  def user_scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    user_scope_fixture(user)
  end

  def user_scope_fixture(user) do
    Scope.for_user(user)
  end

  def set_password(user) do
    {:ok, {user, _expired_tokens}} =
      Users.update_user_password(user, %{password: valid_user_password()})

    user
  end

  def extract_user_token(fun) do
    {:ok, captured_email} = fun.(&"[TOKEN]#{&1}[TOKEN]")

    # `fun` delivers through the real mailer (Swoosh's test adapter), so
    # this confirmation/login email it just sent is sitting in the
    # calling process's mailbox — an internal detail of building a
    # confirmed fixture user, not something the spec itself sent. Left
    # there, it's the *oldest* `{:email, _}` message, and
    # `assert_email_sent/1` always matches the oldest one first — so any
    # later, spec-relevant `assert_email_sent` would wrongly match this
    # one instead. Drain it now so it can't shadow that later assertion.
    receive do
      {:email, ^captured_email} -> :ok
    after
      0 -> :ok
    end

    [_, token | _] = String.split(captured_email.text_body, "[TOKEN]")
    token
  end

  def override_token_authenticated_at(token, authenticated_at) when is_binary(token) do
    CleanerCrm.Repo.update_all(
      from(t in Users.UserToken,
        where: t.token == ^token
      ),
      set: [authenticated_at: authenticated_at]
    )
  end

  def generate_user_magic_link_token(user) do
    {encoded_token, user_token} = Users.UserToken.build_email_token(user, "login")
    CleanerCrm.Repo.insert!(user_token)
    {encoded_token, user_token.token}
  end

  def offset_user_token(token, amount_to_add, unit) do
    dt = DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(:second), amount_to_add, unit)

    CleanerCrm.Repo.update_all(
      from(ut in Users.UserToken, where: ut.token == ^token),
      set: [inserted_at: dt, authenticated_at: dt]
    )
  end
end

defmodule Swoosh.Adapters.Test do
  @moduledoc ~S"""
  An adapter that sends emails as messages to the current process.

  This is meant to be used during tests and works with the assertions found in
  the [Swoosh.TestAssertions](Swoosh.TestAssertions.html) module.

  For feature, browser, and E2E tests where the email is delivered from
  request-handling or LiveView processes, use the
  [Swoosh.Adapters.Sandbox](Swoosh.Adapters.Sandbox.html) adapter instead.

  ## Example

      # config/test.exs
      config :sample, Sample.Mailer,
        adapter: Swoosh.Adapters.Test

      # lib/sample/mailer.ex
      defmodule Sample.Mailer do
        use Swoosh.Mailer, otp_app: :sample
      end
  """

  use Swoosh.Adapter

  def deliver(email, _config) do
    for pid <- pids() do
      send(pid, {:email, email})
    end

    {:ok, %{}}
  end

  def deliver_many(emails, _config) do
    for pid <- pids() do
      send(pid, {:emails, emails})
    end

    responses = for _email <- emails, do: %{}

    {:ok, responses}
  end

  # Essentially finds all of the processes that tried to send an email (in the test)
  # and sends an email to that process.
  defp pids do
    if pid = Application.get_env(:swoosh, :shared_test_process) do
      [pid]
    else
      Enum.uniq([self() | List.wrap(Process.get(:"$callers"))])
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PortalLive.InvoicesTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.ClientsFixtures
  import Swoosh.TestAssertions

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Billing
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  defp owner_scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)
    {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co"})
    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp portal_conn(client) do
    build_conn()
    |> init_test_session(%{})
    |> put_session(:portal_client_id, client.id)
  end

  defp completed_job_fixture(scope, client) do
    {:ok, job} =
      Scheduling.create_job(scope, %{
        client_id: client.id,
        scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), -1),
        start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
        status: :completed
      })

    job
  end

  test "lists invoices with their amounts and statuses" do
    scope = owner_scope_fixture()
    client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Morgan Blake"})

    paid_job = completed_job_fixture(scope, client)
    {:ok, paid} = Billing.create_invoice(scope, %{job_id: paid_job.id, amount_cents: 15_000, status: :paid})

    unpaid_job = completed_job_fixture(scope, client)
    {:ok, unpaid} = Billing.create_invoice(scope, %{job_id: unpaid_job.id, amount_cents: 20_000})

    {:ok, invoices_live, _html} = live(portal_conn(client), ~p"/portal/invoices")

    assert has_element?(invoices_live, "[data-test='invoice-row-#{paid.id}']", "$150.00")
    assert has_element?(invoices_live, "[data-test='invoice-row-#{paid.id}']", "Paid")
    assert has_element?(invoices_live, "[data-test='invoice-row-#{unpaid.id}']", "$200.00")
    assert has_element?(invoices_live, "[data-test='invoice-row-#{unpaid.id}']", "Unpaid")
  end

  test "pays an invoice with a new card, saves it on file, and emails a receipt" do
    scope = owner_scope_fixture()
    client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Morgan Blake", card_on_file: false})
    job = completed_job_fixture(scope, client)
    {:ok, invoice} = Billing.create_invoice(scope, %{job_id: job.id, amount_cents: 15_000})

    {:ok, invoices_live, _html} = live(portal_conn(client), ~p"/portal/invoices")

    invoices_live
    |> element("[data-test='invoice-#{invoice.id}-pay-button']")
    |> render_click()

    invoices_live
    |> form("[data-test='invoice-#{invoice.id}-payment-form']",
      payment: %{card_token: "pm_card_visa", save_card: "true"}
    )
    |> render_submit()

    assert has_element?(invoices_live, "[data-test='card-on-file-badge']")
    assert_email_sent(to: client.email)
  end

  test "a tip added at payment reaches the assigned cleaner's earnings" do
    scope = owner_scope_fixture()
    cleaner = CleanerCrm.SchedulingFixtures.cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)
    client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Morgan Blake"})
    job = completed_job_fixture(scope, client)
    {:ok, job} = Scheduling.assign_cleaner(scope, job, cleaner.id)
    {:ok, invoice} = Billing.create_invoice(scope, %{job_id: job.id, amount_cents: 15_000})

    {:ok, invoices_live, _html} = live(portal_conn(client), ~p"/portal/invoices")

    invoices_live
    |> element("[data-test='invoice-#{invoice.id}-pay-button']")
    |> render_click()

    invoices_live
    |> form("[data-test='invoice-#{invoice.id}-payment-form']",
      payment: %{card_token: "pm_card_visa", tip_cents: "1000"}
    )
    |> render_submit()

    period = CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.current_pay_period(scope)
    assert CleanerCrm.Portal.tip_cents_for_cleaner(scope, cleaner.id, period) == 1_000
  end
end

content.text:
The Portal slice (stories 850, 851, 852) is complete and verified. Summary of what was built:

**Schemas** (`lib/cleaner_crm/portal/`): `portal_session.ex` (hashed magic-link tokens, mirroring `Users.UserToken`'s scheme), `cancellation_policy.ex`, `tip.ex` — plus matching migrations in `priv/repo/migrations/20260708200110-30_*.exs`.

**Context** (`lib/cleaner_crm/portal.ex`): magic-link issuance/exchange, upcoming visits and service history with proof-of-work, reschedule/cancel with cancellation-fee calculation and cleaner/office notifications, invoice listing and payment (card save + tip recording), and `tip_cents_for_cleaner/3` for the earnings read path.

**Web layer**: `PortalController`/`PortalHTML` (magic-link exchange), `PortalAuth` (session-based `on_mount`, no user login), and `PortalLive.Home`/`Visit`/`Invoices`.

**Coordinated shared-file edits (all append-only)**: router.ex (portal routes, clearly commented block), `lib/cleaner_crm.ex` (Portal exports), a one-line `Scheduling.set_cancellation_policy/2` delegate, and an additive/defensive tip-cents read wired into `FieldLive.EarningsComponent` (same optional-dependency pattern already used for Notifications).

**Bug fix**: `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3` was silently dropping its `name:` attr because `Users.register_user/1`'s changeset never casts `:name` — fixed by setting it directly after registration, matching how `Scheduling.register_cleaner/2` already does it for real cleaners.

**Verified**: `MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors` clean (including the boundary compiler). `PORT=4002 mix spex` for all of 850/851/852: 21/21 green. My own 46 new unit/context/LiveView tests: green.

One caveat: a full `mix test` run currently shows a handful of unrelated failures in Scheduling/Users tests. I traced these to a database-hygiene issue of my own making — an early debugging script briefly set the Ecto Sandbox to non-transactional mode before I converted it to a proper test, leaving a few rows permanently committed in the shared test database, which throws off some unscoped count assertions elsewhere in the suite. I flagged this to the team lead with the exact cleanup needed, since the harness's permission system blocked me from running the DELETE myself (mutating shared multi-agent state without explicit consent) — I did not attempt to work around that block. None of this touches Portal code or logic.
